packets.title: glia_activation PprIndex: the PPR index (CSR incidences, out-weights, dangling list) built once per (graph, config) and run per seed set, bit-identical to ppr_vector; ppr_vector, ActivationPlan and activate() run through it; ActivationPlan::run_indexed / rank_indexed and activate_indexed take a prebuilt one; vector_weighted runs a weighted personalisation (the find shape's seeding)
packets.area: EA PPR index (item 5, activation half)
packets.rationale: 0.5.3 item 5 (next-leap-0.5.3.md Scope table: 'keep the PPR index between calls | about 3x faster, bit-identical scores'). At HEAD b3fc2ac7 every PPR answer rebuilds its index per call: activation/src/lib.rs `ppr_vector` builds `id_to_idx` (a HashMap over every node), `incoming: Vec<Vec<(usize, f64)>>` and `out_weight` from the whole edge list, then iterates; ActivationPlan's Pass::execute (activation/src/plan.rs) calls it on every run / rank, so blast_radius (graph/src/blast.rs blast_radius_over -> plan.rank), pack (engine/src/pack.rs run -> MergedGraph::activate -> glia_activation::activate) and resolve each pay O(E) hash lookups before the first iteration. The harness already measured the split: engine/examples/rank_eval.rs `struct Ppr` builds the same incidence lists once per (direction, weights) (`Ppr::build`) and runs `Ppr::power` per query, and its doc says it replicates `glia_activation::ppr_vector`'s arithmetic in its operation order, verified against ActivationPlan::run. This packet lands that split in the activation crate so the engine (EA.2) can hold an index across calls; nothing changes any score.

activation/src/lib.rs - `pub(crate) fn ppr_vector` becomes `PprIndex::build(node_ids, edges, config).vector(seeds)`; new `pub fn activate_indexed(index: &PprIndex, edges: &[Edge], seeds: &[NodeId], config: &ActivationConfig) -> ActivationResult`

activation/src/plan.rs - `ActivationPlan::run_indexed(&self, g: &G, index: &PprIndex, seeds: &[NodeId]) -> ActivatedView` and `rank_indexed(&self, g: &G, index: &PprIndex, seeds: &[NodeId], candidates: &[NodeId]) -> ActivatedView`; Pass::execute gains `index: Option<&PprIndex>`; the debug `Marker` (struct at plan.rs `struct Marker<'a>`) gains a trailing ` index=prebuilt|built` field, printed LAST so the existing prefix of the line is unchanged
packets.implementation:
1. activation/src/ppr_index.rs (new). `#[derive(Debug, Clone)] pub struct PprIndex { node_ids: Vec<NodeId>, id_to_idx: HashMap<NodeId, usize>, start: Vec<usize>, inc: Vec<(usize, f64)>, out_w: Vec<f64>, dangling: Vec<usize>, damping: f64, direction: Direction, weights: Vec<(EdgeCategoryId, u64)>, max_iterations: usize, epsilon: f64 }`. `id_to_idx` is lookup-only (never iterated). `weights` is the config's edge_weights as (category, f64::to_bits) sorted by category id, the fingerprint `matches` compares.
   - `pub fn build<'e>(node_ids: &[NodeId], edges: impl Iterator<Item = &'e Edge>, config: &ActivationConfig) -> Self`: `id_to_idx` collected exactly as ppr_vector does (`node_ids.iter().enumerate().map(|(i, &id)| (id, i)).collect()`, so a repeated id maps to its LAST index and an earlier occurrence scores 0 - ppr_vector's documented rule). Walk the edges in iterator order with ppr_vector's weight rule (`edge_weights.get(&cat).copied().unwrap_or(1.0)`, skip `w <= 0.0`, skip an edge with an endpoint that is no node) and push events `(target, source, w)` in ppr_vector's push order: Forward `(ti, fi)` with `out_w[fi] += w`; Backward `(fi, ti)` with `out_w[ti] += w`; Undirected `(ti, fi)` then `(fi, ti)`, `out_w[fi] += w` then `out_w[ti] += w`. Then CSR by target: `start` prefix sums, a cursor pass that places each event in input order (so each target's incidences are in exactly the order ppr_vector's `incoming[i].push` produced). `dangling = (0..n).filter(|&j| out_w[j] == 0.0).collect()` (index order, as ppr_vector's per-iteration filter sums).
   - `pub fn vector(&self, seeds: &[NodeId]) -> (Vec<f64>, usize)`: ppr_vector's tail verbatim in the same operation order: empty `(Vec::new(), 0)` when n == 0, seeds empty or no seed is a node; personalization `1.0 / seed_count` (seed_count = seeds that are nodes, duplicates counted as ppr_vector counts them: it filters `seeds.iter()` by `contains_key`, so a seed listed twice counts twice and its slot is assigned twice); `d = damping.clamp(0.01, 0.99)`; per iteration `dangling_sum` = sum over `dangling` in index order; `new_scores[i] = (1.0 - d) * personalization[i] + d * (propagated + dangling_sum * personalization[i])` with `propagated` summed over `inc[start[i]..start[i+1]]` as `if out_w[j] > 0.0 { scores[j] * w / out_w[j] } else { 0.0 }`; diff = L1 in index order; stop when `diff < epsilon`; at most max_iterations. Allocate `new_scores` once and swap (bit-identical: every slot is overwritten each iteration).
   - `pub fn node_ids(&self) -> &[NodeId]`, `pub fn index_of(&self, id: NodeId) -> Option<usize>` (the id_to_idx lookup: a repeated id answers its LAST index, the slot ppr_vector scores; EA.4 reads a node's score through it exactly as rank_eval's `node_ppr` does), `pub fn len(&self) -> usize`, `pub fn is_empty(&self)`, `pub fn incidences(&self) -> usize` (inc.len()), and `pub fn matches(&self, config: &ActivationConfig) -> bool`: damping bits, direction, max_iterations, epsilon bits and the sorted weight fingerprint equal (top_k and node_specificity are post-PPR, not part of the index).
2. activation/src/lib.rs: `pub mod ppr_index; pub use ppr_index::PprIndex;`. ppr_vector's body becomes `PprIndex::build(node_ids, edges, config).vector(seeds)` after its existing early return (n == 0 or seeds empty), so there is ONE implementation and the existing plan oracle test (plan.rs: it compares f64 bits of `activate()` against the pre-plan arithmetic) now pins PprIndex. Add `pub fn activate_indexed(index: &PprIndex, edges: &[Edge], seeds: &[NodeId], config: &ActivationConfig) -> ActivationResult`: `activate`'s answer (the hook-free pass, Universe::Reached, sorted, top_k) with the vector from the index; `edges` is read only when `config.node_specificity != Specificity::None` (the degree specificity needs them) and is the slice `activate` would have been given - a caller with Specificity::None may pass `&[]`.
3. activation/src/plan.rs: Pass::execute(g, seeds, universe, mode) gains `index: Option<&PprIndex>`. With `Some(ix)`: the node list is `ix.node_ids()` (g.node_ids() is NOT called) and the vector is `ix.vector(seeds)`; when `!ix.matches(config)` the pass ignores the index (computes as today) and prints `[activation] index mismatch mode=<mode>` unconditionally on stderr (a caller bug made visible, never a wrong score). Specificity still reads `g.edges()`. `run` / `rank` pass None; new `run_indexed` / `rank_indexed` pass Some. The debug Marker (GLIA_ACTIVATION_DEBUG=1) gains a LAST field: the line ends `.. synth_cells=N index=prebuilt|built` (`index=built` also for mode=activate / synthesize, which build none: say `index=none` there). Update the pinned Display test in plan.rs's tests (the `marker.to_string()` assertion that spells `[activation] plan mode=rank signals=[degree_specificity] filters=[live] synth=[] universe=5712 kept=812 dropped=[live:37] synth_cells=0`) to the new trailing field; the prefix stays byte-identical, so a reader grepping `plan mode=rank` is unaffected.
4. Tests (in ppr_index.rs and plan.rs `mod tests`): (a) for each Direction x damping in {0.5, 0.85} x a graph with a dangling node, a zero-weight category, a repeated node id, an edge to a non-node and a self-loop: `PprIndex::build(..).vector(seeds)` equals the pre-change ppr_vector body (keep a private copy of HEAD's ppr_vector as `#[cfg(test)] fn ppr_vector_head` the oracle) in f64 bits and iteration count; (b) one index, three different seed sets in sequence: each equals a fresh build's vector in bits (no state leaks between runs); (c) `rank_indexed` / `run_indexed` views equal `rank` / `run` (scores bits, order, iterations, dropped) with a filter and a signal registered; (d) `matches` is false after changing damping, direction or one weight, and a mismatched index gives the unindexed answer.

INTEGRATOR NOTE (0.5.3 merge): add `pub fn vector_weighted(&self, pers: &[(NodeId, f64)]) -> (Vec<f64>, usize)` beside `vector`: the same tail, but the personalisation is filled as rank_eval's `Ppr::power` fills it (`personalization[idx] = w` for each (node, w) in the given order, so a repeated node keeps its LAST weight; no normalisation; a node that is not in the index is skipped; empty after the skip -> `(vec![0.0; n], 0)` exactly as `power` returns zeros, NOT the empty vector `vector` returns, because the find shape's callers pool by index). `vector(seeds)` stays ppr_vector's arithmetic (uniform 1 / seed_count). Test (e): `vector_weighted` with weights 1/k on k distinct seeds equals `vector` on those seeds in f64 bits; a weighted case equals a private copy of rank_eval's `Ppr::power` on the same incidences in f64 bits. Consumers: EA.4 `base_keys` (EC.4's bank, EC.13's PX1 / PXT, which r3_transfer seeds with `q.w[i] / |nodes|` per node).

packets.title: engine::rank slot: Ranking { base: RankBase::{Ppr, PprWide, Bfs}, cochange_first } naming the measured structure rankers P1 / PT* / B0 and their co-change-first forms H10 / H10[PT*] / H10[B0], STRUCTURE_CANDIDATES (SELs0's set for item 10), and RankCache: the long-lived holder of PPR indexes, the file index, the carry adjacency and the co-change index, with a graph-shape guard and the `[rank-cache]` marker
packets.area: EA ranking candidates + PPR index cache (items 1 and 5, engine half)
packets.rationale: Item 1 (PPR damping 0.85 + sum pooling per file) is measured as a candidate, not a default: round 3 (dev-notes/ranking-eval-round3-2026-10-19.md; scoreboard row 31) found PT* - P1 -0.035 [-0.052, -0.019] on commons-lang and +0.019 on commons-io, and next-leap-0.5.3.md's round-3 scope note says item 1 'reaches the answers through item 4's selection, not as a fixed default alone'. So the answers need a named, selectable ranking with exactly the harness's definitions (engine/examples/rank_eval.rs): P1 = undirected PPR at CODE_TABLES.activation_config(None) (damping 0.5) seeded uniformly over every node of the seed files, max-pooled per file (`base_cfg`, `Ppr::uniform`, `file_pool(.., false)`); PT* = the same at damping 0.85 with sum pooling (`r1_tune_indexes` grid entry `base,d85`, picked with `--pick base,d85`, `file_pool(.., true)`); B0 = carry-edge BFS in both directions from the seed files' nodes, key [-depth, file degree] (`bfs_key`); and their co-change-first forms H10 = [C0, P1], H10[PT*] = [C0, PT*], H10[B0] = [C0, -depth, degree] (`run_query`, `r3_transfer`). Item 10's structure-only selection SELs0 is {P1, PT*, B0} (rank_eval.rs `r3_sets`), and EC (items 4 / 10, EC.4 / EC.8 / EC.9) calls EA's rankers by these names, so B0 is EA's too (EC.4: 'call EA's file ranker for name ... B0'). Item 5's index needs a holder that outlives one call: RankCache.

Both signals live on the harness's FILE SPACE, `index_graph`: a candidate file is the located file of a MODULE node with no ORIGIN cell containing `generated`, whose extension (`ext_of`: after the basename's last '.', non-empty stem, ASCII-lowercased) is non-empty and not in NOT_CODE (38 extensions: md, json, yaml, toml, lock, html, css, ...), paths sorted; ties go to the smaller index, i.e. the smaller path (`better`). Its C0 is unfloored and counted over that space: `git log --no-merges --no-renames --name-only` mapped through `pidx` (paths present at the graph's head), a training commit keeps 1..=MAX_FILES (30) MAPPED files (`train_ok`), `cnt[a] += 1` per file and `co[a][b] += 1` per ordered pair a != b, and a seed's C0 is `co[s][f] / (cnt[s] + 1)` (`let denom = f64::from(cnt[sd as usize]) + 1.0`), summed over the seed files in the review shape (`r3_tqueries`). The draft read the history stage's `module_files` (every MODULE file, docs and config included, so both the denominators and the 30-file eligibility moved) and the rename fold `commit_file_sets` (which credits a file with commits made under its old name: the harness never did); both are unmeasured and are replaced by the harness's rule. The graph's CO_CHANGES edges cannot supply C0 either: LF.5b keeps pairs with support >= 3 and >= 300 per mille, at most 5000 (engine/src/external/history.rs MIN_SUPPORT / MIN_RATIO_PERMILLE / MAX_PAIRS). Reading the snapshot at query time is what cochange_multi already does (engine/src/cochange.rs); nothing is computed inside a build. EC.2's leak-free replay counts the same thing commit by commit, so the counting rule and C0 are one trait here, implemented by both.

packets.area: EA file ranking (items 1 and 2, logic)
packets.rationale: rank_eval ranks FILES, over every candidate file, from PPR seeded at the seed FILES: `pers = Ppr::uniform(&seed_ppr)` over every node of the seed file(s) (run_query; the review shape's r3_transfer: `Ppr::uniform(&nodes)` over every seed file's nodes), the UNDIRECTED base config (`base_cfg = undirected(None, Direction::Undirected)`), node scores pooled over every node of each file (`file_pool`), keys compared lexicographically by `better` with ties to the smaller file index. The draft instead pooled blast radius's own PPR, which is directional (graph/src/blast.rs blast_radius_over: Backward for a backward radius), seeded at the seed NODES only, and scored over the closure only, then capped co-change-only files at an unmeasured 20 and compared with total_cmp: four departures from the measured ranker. This packet computes the measured key itself, so the answer's `files` IS the ranking rank_eval scored (recall@10 / MRR), and EA.9 proves it bit for bit against the harness. The engine's answers list NODES, so one function (order_rows) turns the file ranking into a row order; EC.8 / EC.9 hand their selected base to the same two functions.

      - Ppr / PprWide: `cfg = CODE_TABLES.activation_config(None)`, `cfg.direction = Direction::Undirected`, `cfg.top_k = usize::MAX`, `cfg.damping = base.damping()` (0.5 / WIDE_DAMPING): rank_eval's `base_cfg` and its `base,d85` grid entry exactly. `ix = cache.ppr_index(merged, SourceKey::Merged, &cfg)`; `(v, _) = ix.vector(&seed_nodes)` (EA.1; bit-identical to rank_eval's `Ppr::run(&Ppr::uniform(..))`: same build order, same personalisation 1/len, same iteration). Per file f: `acc = 0.0`; for u in files.nodes(f) in order: `s = ix.index_of(u).map_or(0.0, |i| v.get(i).copied().unwrap_or(0.0))`; Ppr `acc = acc.max(s)`, PprWide `acc += s` (rank_eval `file_pool`, verbatim).
      - Bfs: `adj = cache.carry(merged)`; `b = algo::reach::bfs(&adj, &seed_nodes, Walk::Both, usize::MAX)`; depth[f] = min depth of a reached node located in f (f64::INFINITY when none) - rank_eval `bfs_key`.
   c. c0 = when `ranking.cochange_first`: `rank::c0(&*cache.cochange(merged), seed_files, n)` (EA.3), else zeros.
   d. keys[f]: P1 / PT* `[base, 0, 0]` (rank_eval `scalar`); B0 `[if depth finite { -depth } else { -1e9 }, files.degree(f), 0]`; H10 / H10[PT*] `[c0, base, 0]` (`lex2`); H10[B0] `[c0, -depth or -1e9, degree]` (r3 `push("H10[B0]", ..)`).
   e. order = every f not in seed_files, sorted with rank_eval's `better` copied verbatim (`a[i] > b[i]` / `a[i] < b[i]` on f64 for i in 0..3, then `ia < ib`) as the comparator (`Ordering::Less` when better(a, b)). Index order is (repo label, path) order (EA.3), so every tie goes to the smaller path: never a NodeId.
   f. One marker line per call (see fired_on_marker): `seed_files`, `candidates` = n, `cochange_files` = files with c0 > 0 outside the seeds, `index` = the ppr_index result (or `bfs`).
2. `FileRanking::top(files, k, rows_per_file)`: the first k of `order` as RankedFile { rank (1-based), file, repo label, cochange = c0[f], ppr = Some(base) for Ppr / PprWide else None, depth = Some(d) for Bfs when reached else None, rows = rows_per_file.get(f) or 0 }.
3. `order_rows(row_files, seed_files, fr)`: the permutation the answer applies to its rows (row_files[i] = the candidate file of row i, or None), or None when it is the identity. Each row gets a tier and a sort key:
   - tier 0 (lifted): `fr.ranking.cochange_first` and its file f has c0[f] > 0 and is no seed file: key = fr.position(f) (which already orders c0 desc, then the base key, then path).
   - tier 1: every other row. Base Ppr: no key (input order: the answer's own 0.5.2 order stands, so `Ranking::head()` and a history-free repo are byte-identical, and EC.8's pick P1 is the pre-EC order as EC requires). Base PprWide / Bfs: rows of a seed file first (the change's own file, which the measured ranking leaves out), then rows of a candidate file by fr.position(f), then rows with no candidate file (docs, config) last.
   Ties inside a key keep the input order (a stable sort on (tier, key), the input index last). No float is compared here: positions are integers.
4. packets.title: rank_eval proves the port: `--engine-parity on` checks FileIndex against the harness's candidate files and the engine's rank_files keys against P1 / PT* / B0 / H10 / H10[PT*] / H10[B0] per query, fed the harness's leak-free prefix co-change counts; and the ANS:impact / ANS:pack gate rankers get the same per-query co-change, so the rank gate scores the shipped co-change path
packets.area: EA harness parity + gate wiring (items 1, 2, 5)
packets.rationale: The scope's gate ('rank_eval runs as a release check ... a ranking change that lowers recall@10 or MRR beyond its CI fails') scores harness rankers; EG.1 adds ANS:impact / ANS:pack rankers that call the engine's diff_impact_from_diff / pack_ids, but its risks say an answer reading history sees none in the gate (the --repo copy holds no `.glia/`) and that 'a later packet whose answer reads history must give its ANS ranker that snapshot built in memory from commits strictly older than the test commit'. Co-change is that answer: without this packet the gate never sees items 2's effect, and nothing proves EA.3 / EA.4 compute what rank_eval measured. This packet closes both: a parity mode that compares the engine's rankings with the harness's on every query (bit for bit on the single-seed shape), and the ANS rankers fed the harness's own leak-free prefix counts through CochangeIndex::from_counts (EA.3) and RankCache::with_cochange.
entry_points: engine/examples/rank_eval.rs - new flag `--engine-parity on|off` (default off); `fn engine_parity(ctx, g, queries, tqs, cnt_at, co_at) -> serde_json::Value`; the ANS rankers' BlastOptions / PackArgs gain `rank_cache = Some(Arc::new(RankCache::new("answer", &BTreeMap::new(), &BTreeMap::new()).with_cochange(CochangeIndex::from_counts(..))))` built per test commit
packets.implementation:
Prerequisites: the private-config scrub of rank_eval.rs (next-leap-0.5.3.md Order 1) has landed and EG.1 (the ANS rankers, the REF_* pin) is in; build on both, add nothing domain-specific.
1. File space parity (once per run, before any query): `let fi = glia_engine::rank::FileIndex::of(&merged, &BTreeMap::new());` assert `fi.len() == g.paths.len()` and `fi.path(i) == g.paths[i]` for every i, and `glia_engine::rank::NOT_CODE_EXTS == NOT_CODE`; print `[rank-parity] files harness=<n> engine=<m> equal=<true|false> not_code_equal=<b>`; a mismatch with `--engine-parity on` panics with the first differing index (the parity is meaningless on two file spaces).
2. Prefix counts: at each test commit the harness already holds `cnt` and `co` (strictly older training commits, the leak-free state q.c0 reads). Snapshot them into `CochangeIndex::from_counts(cnt.clone(), co_sorted)` where co_sorted[f] = co[f] as (g, n) sorted by g (co is a HashMap per file: sort, never iterate it into output). Build it once per test commit (not per query), only when `--engine-parity on` or `--ans on`.
3. Parity rows (`--engine-parity on`): per single-seed query q, `cache = RankCache::new("parity", ..).with_cochange(prefix)`; for each of the six Rankings (Ranking { base, cochange_first } over STRUCTURE_CANDIDATES x {false, true}) call `rank_files(&merged, &cache, &[q.seed], &[], r)` with r = `Ranking::new(base, cochange)` and compare `keys` with the harness's keys for `r.harness_name()` (P1 / PT* from `--pick base,d85` (assert ctx.pick names `base,d85` when parity is on) / B0 / H10 / H10[PT*] / H10[B0]) in f64 bits over every non-seed file, and `order` with the harness's `order(&key, seed)`. For the review shapes (tqs, shapes 0-2) the same over q.seeds in the harness's seed order, comparing keys with a relative tolerance of 1e-12 on the c0 component only (k-seed sums) and exactly elsewhere. Count per (shape, ranking): `[rank-parity] label=<l> shape=<single|k2|k3|half> ranking=<name> queries=<n> key_mismatch=<k> order_mismatch=<o>`; the JSON gets `engine_parity: {shape: {ranking: {queries, key_mismatch, order_mismatch}}}`. A non-zero key_mismatch on the single shape panics at the end of the run (after the report is written) with the first differing (query, file).
4. ANS rankers see co-change (always, when `--ans on`): the BlastOptions passed to diff_impact_from_diff and the PackArgs passed to pack_ids get `rank_cache = Some(Arc::new(cache_with_prefix))` built from step 2's per-test-commit index (Ranking::default() = H10 order). Without step 4 the ANS rankers would compute co-change-free answers (no `.glia/` in the copy) and the gate could not see item 2.
5. Report: the md gains a `## Engine parity` table (shape x ranking: queries, key mismatches, order mismatches) when on.

packets.title: `glia_activation::algo::fuse`: domain-free rank fusion over per-candidate score vectors: min-max over candidates, blends, equal means and the lexicographic LX order (typed links first), every tie broken by a caller-given total order
packets.area: EB fusion primitives (item 7: LX)
packets.rationale: Items 3, 6 and 7 need one fusion vocabulary shared by review and find: H9s50 = 0.5 mm(T1s) + 0.5 mm(P1), LX[IDR, X] = order by IDR, then X. rank_eval implements these as `minmax` (candidates = every file but the seed; a flat vector is all zeros), `blend`, `r3_eq`, `lex2` and `better` / `order` (keys compared lexicographically, ties to the lower file index). Round 2 table A: LX[IDR,H9s50] 0.595 vs the min-max blend H9si 0.592 on Kina, glia 0.934 vs 0.881 (item 7). Generic ranking math belongs in activation::algo (CLAUDE.md Key Design Decisions), not in the engine; the engine adds the code reading (which files, which signals).

packets.implementation:
New module (the E0 slot declares `pub mod fuse;` in activation/src/algo/mod.rs; this packet fills the file). Items, all pure, no allocation beyond the returned Vec, no HashMap:
- `pub fn minmax(v: &[f64], excluded: &[bool]) -> Vec<f64>`: lo / hi over the indices with `!excluded[i]`; when `!(hi > lo)` (flat, empty, or every entry excluded) every output is 0.0; else `(v[i] - lo) / (hi - lo)` for every i (an excluded index still gets a value; callers never rank it). Exactly rank_eval's `minmax` / `mm_ex` arithmetic. Non-finite input is a debug_assert and maps to 0.0 in release.
- `pub fn blend(a: f64, x: &[f64], y: &[f64]) -> Vec<f64>` = `a * x[i] + (1.0 - a) * y[i]`.
- `pub fn mean(parts: &[&[f64]]) -> Vec<f64>` = the per-index sum / parts.len() (rank_eval `r3_eq`).
- `pub fn lex_order(keys: &[&[f64]], tie: &[u32], excluded: &[bool]) -> Vec<usize>`: the non-excluded indices best first: compare `keys[0][i]` ... `keys[k-1][i]` descending with plain `>` / `<` (rank_eval `better`: equal values, -0.0 and 0.0 included, fall through to the next key; `total_cmp` would order -0.0 below 0.0 and diverge from the harness), then `tie[i]` ascending (the caller's total order: the engine passes each file's position in path order, so no NodeId and no hash order reaches an output). Panics in debug when lengths differ.
- `pub fn order(score: &[f64], tie: &[u32], excluded: &[bool]) -> Vec<usize>` = `lex_order(&[score], ..)`.
- `pub fn lx(typed: &[f64], rest: &[&[f64]], tie: &[u32], excluded: &[bool]) -> Vec<usize>` = `lex_order` with `typed` first (item 7's name for it in the docs).
Marker: under `GLIA_ALGO_DEBUG=1` (the crate's private `algo_debug()` reader in activation/src/algo/mod.rs, visible to this child module), `lex_order` prints `[algo] fuse keys=<k> candidates=<n> excluded=<e> zero_first_key=<z>` once per call (z = candidates whose first key is 0, i.e. ordered by the rest). Module doc: the definitions above, the source of each in rank_eval (ranker names H9s50, LX[..], H18s), and the rule that a fusion never adds a candidate: a key of all zeros leaves the rest of the order to the next key. Unit tests in the file: (1) minmax of [3, 1, 2] with index 0 excluded -> [2.0, 0.0, 1.0]; flat -> zeros; (2) blend / mean arithmetic; (3) lex_order on keys ([1,0,0,1], [0.2,0.9,0.9,0.1]) with tie [3,2,1,0] -> [0, 3, 2, 1] (index 0 beats 3 on the second key, 0.2 > 0.1; indices 1 and 2 tie on both keys and go to the lower tie value, index 2); (3b) keys ([0.0], [-0.0]) compare equal and fall to the tie; (4) excluded indices never appear; (5) a fixed 6-entry vector set copied from rank_eval's H9s50 / LX[IDR,H9s50] arithmetic gives the same order as the harness functions (values written inline in the test, not imported).

2. code-domain/src/glia_config.rs: `pub struct IdPattern` parsed from a shape string: `{U}` = one ASCII uppercase letter then zero or more ASCII uppercase letters / digits; `{N}` = one or more ASCII digits; `{N<k>}` (k 1..=9) = exactly k digits; `{l?}` = an optional single ASCII lowercase letter; any other char a literal, matched case-sensitively. A pattern must contain one `{N}` / `{N<k>}`, be 1..=64 chars and name no unknown `{..}`. Matching is a hand-written backtracking matcher over bytes (patterns are tiny), word-bounded: the byte before the match and the byte after it are not `[A-Za-z0-9_]` (a following `.` or `-` is a boundary only when the byte after it is not a digit, so `DT.5h` matches in `DT.5h:` but `{U}-{N}` does not match inside `UTF-8x`). `{U}` is greedy with backtracking. Letter shorthands (rank_eval `dot_ids`), only for a pattern ending in `{l?}` whose match ended in a lowercase letter: `X.5a/b` also yields `X.5b`, `X.5a-c` / `X.5a–c` / `X.5h-X.5l` also yield every letter up to the end letter (at most 20 letters past the start), each extra mention at the shorthand's byte span. engine/src/intent/ids.rs re-exports nothing of the grammar and holds `pub struct IdMention { pub id: String, pub family: String /* the matched text before its first digit group: `T`, `FR-`, `DT.` */, pub start: usize, pub end: usize /* byte offsets */ }`. `pub struct IdVocab { patterns, local_words, trackers }`; `pub const DEFAULT_PATTERNS: [&str; 2] = ["{U}-{N}", "T{N3}"]` (tickets and spec-kit requirement / success ids; spec-kit task ids) and `pub const DEFAULT_LOCAL_WORDS: [&str; 5] = ["analysis", "finding", "remediation", "review", "audit"]`; `IdVocab::for_root(root: &Path) -> IdVocab` reads `glia_config::load(root)` (a config with `patterns` set REPLACES the defaults; `patterns = []` turns id routing off). `pub fn mentions(&self, text: &str) -> Vec<IdMention>`: every pattern over the text, overlapping matches resolved longest-first then earliest, returned sorted by start, deduped. `pub fn report(&self, label, surface)` prints the marker.

packets.implementation:
In engine/src/intent/defs.rs, after EB.5a's reader:
1. `pub struct Namespaces` built by `IdDefs::namespaces(&self, local_words: &[String]) -> Namespaces`. A SERIES is (page, family) over the doc rows (tracker rows: one series per tracker file, never local, never merged). A series is LOCAL (a findings series) when any of its rows' `heading_words` contains a local word and none of those rows' nearest heading (the section heading) contains `decision`; all rows of a series must agree, else it is exported (rank_eval: `*e = *e && is_local`). RESTATED merge: two exported series of the same family on different pages sharing >= 3 ids whose mean word-multiset Dice over the shared ids' `head` texts is >= 0.3 (the harness's Dice: words = alphanumeric runs, lowercased; empty-vs-empty = 1.0) are united (union-find, iterating series pairs in (page, family) order so the result is order-independent). A component's NAMESPACE name: among members with a scope, the least `<scope>/<file name>`; else the least page path. `Namespaces` holds `by_id: BTreeMap<String, Vec<Series { ns, local, scope, page }>>`, `def: BTreeMap<(page, id), ns>`, `scopes: BTreeMap<ns, BTreeSet<scope>>`, `rows: BTreeMap<(ns, id), Vec<usize /* DefRow index */>>`, and counts (series, local, merges, multi-series ids).
2. `pub struct Ctx<'a> { pub own_page: Option<&'a str>, pub own_scope: Option<&'a str>, pub line_scopes: Vec<String>, pub recent: &'a [String] /* newest first */, pub text: &'a str }` and `pub fn line_scopes(line: &str, ns: &Namespaces) -> Vec<String>`: the scopes the line names: a path token under a scope dir, a token equal to a scope dir's last segment, or a spec-kit number `NNN` adjacent (within one token) to the word `spec` / `specs` naming exactly one `specs/<NNN-..>` scope.
3. `pub struct Resolved { pub id: String, pub ns: String, pub tier: &'static str /* fact|derived|heuristic */, pub route: &'static str }` and `pub fn resolve(&self, id: &str, cx: &Ctx) -> Result<Resolved, &'static str>`, first that applies: own page defines it -> fact `own-page`; no series -> Err `undefined`; visible = series not local, or local with page == own_page or scope == own_scope; none visible -> Err `local-only`; one -> derived `unique`; one visible in the first `line_scopes` entry that has any (an exported one preferred when several) -> derived `line-scope`; own_scope -> derived `own-scope`; exactly one visible series with no scope -> derived `global`; then rank_eval `r2_pick` exactly: POOL = the visible series holding a Pending row for the id, or every visible series when none does; a pool of one -> derived `open-row` when more than one series is visible and exactly one is pending, else `one-left`; else the first `recent` scope (newest first) holding a POOL series -> heuristic `recent-scope`; else the POOL series with the greatest scope name among those whose scope is a spec-kit `specs/` dir (spec-kit numbers sort newest last) -> heuristic `newest-scope`; when none has a spec scope, the least POOL namespace name -> heuristic `newest-scope`. (The draft let recent / newest pick among ALL visible series; the harness restricts both to the pending pool.)
4. `pub fn resolve_line(&self, line: &str, mentions: &[IdMention], cx: &Ctx) -> Vec<Result<Resolved, &'static str>>`: resolves each mention, then the sibling rule: a mention resolved by `recent-scope` / `newest-scope` takes the namespace a same-family mention on the same line got by any other route, when that namespace defines it (route `sibling`, tier derived).
5. Lineage classes (rank_eval `KLin::build` / `exp`): the (new, old) pairs of EB.5a's rows over namespaced keys `<ns>|<id>` (an id resolved in the row's own page context); a pair merges into one class when it is the only partner on both sides, else the old key REDIRECTS to the new one; classes are capped at 6 members (union-find in key order, a merge that would pass the cap is skipped and counted). `pub fn expand(&self, key) -> Vec<String>`: the key's class plus the classes it redirects to, in insertion order. EB.6 routes every member of the expansion.
6. Every Resolved / Err route is counted for the caller's marker (`routes=<route>:<n>,..` in route-name order).
Tests (engine/tests/intent_namespaces.rs over EB.5a-style fixtures): two specs each defining T001 -> a mention from inside `specs/002-x/plan.md` resolves own-scope to 002, an unqualified one with `spec 002` on the line resolves line-scope, with neither and one pending row resolves open-row, with neither and both pending + recent [`specs/001-a`] resolves recent-scope, else newest-scope to 002; a `review-findings.md` series `F1..F5` is local (not visible from another spec); `decisions.md` restating D1-D4 with the same row words on two pages merges into one namespace (D-series mentions on either page resolve to the same ns); `D2/D5` on one line where D2 resolves line-scope and D5 would be newest-scope -> D5 sibling; a single global series -> unique. Pending pool: T001 defined in specs/001-a (done) and specs/002-b (pending) and specs/003-c (pending), recent [`specs/001-a`] -> NOT 001 (not in the pool): newest-scope 003; recent [`specs/002-b`] -> recent-scope 002. Lineage: `T015 (was T009)` one-to-one merges, so a mention of T009 expands to T015's rows; `T020 split into T021` and `T020 split into T022` redirect T020 to both. Every resolution is identical when the pages are enumerated in reverse (order independence).

Globs: braces expanded first (cartesian, at most 64 patterns, rank_eval `kbraces`), then each matched against every candidate with rank_eval `kglob` (`*` / `?` inside a segment, `**` across), at most 30 hits else none. `pub fn block(&self, toks: &[String]) -> Vec<(usize, &'static str, String)>`: rank_eval `block`: tokens in order, a File that is ambiguous by suffix deferred until the block's unique paths give context, Dirs expanded, Globs matched; output sorted by (candidate index, route), deduped. Route counts accumulate for the marker.

packets.title: `glia_engine::intent::idr`: typed id routing (IDR): a text's ids -> the scoped-id resolver (lineage-expanded, families) -> the defining rows -> the files they name (pending 1.0, done 0.5), plus the code whose comments cite the id (0.5); the conventional-commit scope route to feature / spec doc dirs when no id resolves; read at one revision; recent scopes from history subjects
packets.area: EB typed id routing: reach (item 6)
packets.rationale: Round 2 verdict A: IDR = names-file edges of the defining rows (`R2_W_NAMED` 1.0, `R2_W_DONE` 0.5, max per file per id) plus the code citing the id (`R2_W_CITED` 0.5), summed over the subject's resolved ids; `IDRn - IDRc` +0.244 (Kina) / +0.835 (glia) shows the names-file edge carries it; one extra hop through a defining row's mentions costs 0.023 (Kina) and roles-off costs 0.035 / 0.215, so neither is ported. Measured as a no-op where no id resolves (round 2 E, round 3 T). Everything is read at the revision the answer stands on (review: the base, find: the working tree). Three measured parts the draft left out: a key expands to its lineage class before reaching files (`r2_kina_reach` / `r2_glia_commit`: `cl.exp(key)`); an id naming a family resolves to every member (`r2_glia_commit` route `family`: `DT.5` -> `DT.5a`..); and on repos with no id vocabulary IDR is the scope route (`r2_scope_commit`: a subject `feat(billing): ..` -> `**/billing/**/*.md` and `**/NNN-billing/**/*.md` at the parent -> the paths on every line, `- [x]` lines 0.5), which fired on quokka-stack (6 of 6 id subjects reaching a file, round 2 table).

1. engine/src/git_rev.rs: `pub(crate) fn grep_words_at(tree: &Tree, words: &[String], paths: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<(String /*path*/, String /*line*/)>, String>`: Rev = `git grep -I -n --no-color -w -F -e <w>... <sha> -- <pathspecs>` (paths passed through a `--pathspec-from-file=-` stdin list to avoid argv limits), output `<sha>:<path>:<n>:<line>` split on the first three `:`; Work = read each listed file (<= 1 MiB, valid UTF-8 lossily) and keep lines containing a word-bounded occurrence (the same boundary rule as `IdPattern`). Sorted by (path, line).
2. engine/src/intent/idr.rs: `pub struct RoutedId { pub id: String, pub ns: Option<String>, pub tier: Option<&'static str>, pub route: &'static str, pub defined_at: Option<(String, i64)>, pub state: Option<&'static str>, pub named_files: usize, pub cited_files: usize }` (Serialize) and `pub struct Idr { pub ids: Vec<RoutedId>, pub idr: Vec<f64> /* per candidate (EB.3 Candidates order) */, pub named: Vec<f64>, pub cited: Vec<f64>, pub has_id: bool }`.
   `pub fn route(text: &str, side: &IdrSide, recent: &[String]) -> Idr` where `IdrSide { cands: &Candidates, defs: &IdDefs, ns: &Namespaces, vocab: &IdVocab, tree: &Tree }`: mentions = `vocab.mentions(text)` (deduped by id, first occurrence kept); each resolved with `resolve_line` on the line holding it, Ctx { own_page None, own_scope None, line_scopes from that line, recent, text }. An id with no series that is a FAMILY (rank_eval `family`: the defined ids equal to it plus one or two trailing lowercase letters, e.g. `DT.5` -> `DT.5a`..`DT.5l`) resolves to every member, route `family`, tier derived. Each resolved key is expanded through `Namespaces::expand` (EB.5b's lineage classes) and every member key is routed. For a key: NAMED = for every DefRow of the key, `PathResolver::block(row.names)`; weight 1.0 when the row is Pending or has no state, 0.5 when Done; per file the MAX over the key's rows (rank_eval `r2_max`). CITED: `grep_words_at(tree, [id], cands.paths)`, keeping a hit only when the id sits in the line's COMMENT part (rank_eval `kcomment`: a line starting `* `, `#`, `--` or `*/`, else the text from the first `//`, `/*`, `<!--`, ` -- ` or ` # `), so a string literal or an identifier is never a citation; a hit counts for (ns, id) when the id has one series (`unique` / `global` / tracker namespaces), or when `resolve_line` of the citing line with Ctx { own_scope = the scope whose docs name the citing file (any DefRow name resolving to it), line_scopes from the line } returns the same ns; weight 0.5 per file. idr[f] = SUM over resolved keys of (named[f] + cited[f]) (rank_eval `r2_finish`).
   SCOPE ROUTE (rank_eval `r2_scope_commit`), only when no mention resolved: the text's conventional-commit scopes (rank_eval `r2_scopes`: `<letters>(<a>,<b>):` or `!:`, each scope lowercased, >= 3 chars of `[a-z0-9_-]`); for each scope s, the tree's `*.md` files (outside `node_modules/`) with a directory segment equal to s or `NNN-s`; every line of them (fences included, as `git grep` reads them) through `PathResolver::block(kpath_tokens(line))`, weight 0.5 when the trimmed line starts `- [x]`, `- [X]` or `* [x]`, else 1.0, MAX per file per scope, summed over scopes; route `scope-dir`, tier derived, one `RoutedId { id: "scope:<s>", .. }` per scope that has docs. has_id is true when an id resolved or a scope had docs. An unresolved mention (`undefined`, `local-only`) is listed with route = the Err name and contributes nothing.
   `pub fn recent_scopes(subjects_newest_first: &[&str], ns: &Namespaces, vocab: &IdVocab) -> Vec<String>`: rank_eval's recent list (`R2_RECENT` = 5): the subjects processed OLDEST to newest, each subject's mentions resolved with the deque so far and every resolved scope pushed to the front (dedup, truncate 5). Callers pass the subjects of the snapshot commits shaped like rank_eval's test commits (2..=30 candidate files, `test_ok`), with the answer's excluded shas removed; no window cap (the draft's invented 50 is dropped: the harness reads every earlier test commit). Unlike the harness, which resolved each earlier subject at its own parent, they are resolved against the answer's revision (EB.9 measures it).
3. Marker, once per route call: `[idr] repo=<label> surface=<s> rev=<sha12|worktree> ids=<m> resolved=<r> unresolved=<u> routes=<route:n,..> named_files=<n> cited_files=<c> files=<f> recent=<k>`.

packets.rationale: Item 3 (the subject keeps 89-106% of the optimistic text gain on 6 repos; round 3 review shapes k2 / k3 / half: H9s50 - P1 CI above 0 on 5 / 3 / 4 repos) and items 6 + 7 (IDR first holds on every id repo in every review shape: glia +0.528..+0.569, Kina +0.082..+0.101; LX beats min-max blending IDR). packets.title: `glia find <repo> <query> --files` / `PyGraph.find_files`: the files a free-text query is about, LX[IDR, T1s] (typed id links first, then the query's BM25 over past commit messages, ties by file degree then path), one repo, with its routed ids and an absence when neither signal fires
packets.area: EB find intent (items 3, 6, 7)
packets.rationale: Items 3 and 6 name `find` (the query text). find today is a name / qname matcher over nodes (engine/src/find.rs tiers), with no free-text answer. Round 3's find shape (no seed): IDR first holds (glia +0.603, Kina +0.105); the intent blend with PPR is BELOW the text alone in find (H9s50 vs T1s: 0 above, 10 n.s., 2 below), PPR seeded from the text's top files is below the text on 4 of 12, and co-change first is below on 6 of 12. So find's fixed fusion is LX[IDR, T1s] (round 3 find table: glia 0.932, Kina 0.547 vs T1s 0.337 / 0.441), with rank_eval's find-shape tie rule (all-zero keys fall to the file's degree). Item 11 (find's selection set, another group) builds on this answer. A separate `--files` mode keeps find's node answer and its pyo3 return shape untouched.

packets.implementation:
1. engine/src/find.rs: `#[non_exhaustive] pub struct FindFilesOptions { pub top_k: usize /* default DEFAULT_TOP_K */, pub surface: &'static str }`, `#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Serialize)] pub struct FoundFile { pub rank: usize, pub file: String, pub idr: f64, pub text: f64, pub degree: f64, pub ids: Vec<String> }`, `pub const FIND_FILES_FUSION: &str = "LX[IDR,T1s]";` and `pub fn find_files(merged: &MergedGraph, repo_roots: &BTreeMap<u64, String>, query: &str, opts: &FindFilesOptions) -> Result<Answer<FoundFile>, String>`: Err(`find --files ranks one repo's files; got <n> repos`) unless `repo_roots` has exactly one entry. Candidates = EB.3 `candidates(merged, repo)`; text = `TextIndex::load(root, &cands, &BTreeSet::new())` scores of the query (zeros when absent); idr = `idr::route(query, side, recent)` over the working tree (`read_defs(Tree::Work(root), project dirs, vocab, Some((merged, repo)))`, `IdVocab::for_root`, EB.5c's `PathResolver`, recent = `recent_scopes` over the history subjects). Order = `fuse::lex_order(&[&idr, &text, &cands.deg], tie = path position, excluded = none)` (rank_eval find shape: ties in the first keys go to the file degree). Rows = files with idr > 0 or text > 0, in that order, cut at top_k (0 keeps all), rank 1-based, `ids` = the routed ids that reached the file. Empty -> `Answer` with an `Absence` (reason `no_match`, FACT) whose note says which inputs were missing: `no id in the query resolved to a defining row` and/or `no history messages (run glia history sync)` / `no past commit message matches the query`, with the absence caveats empty (no mechanism walked). Determinism: every map BTree, ties by path.
2. cli/src/cmd/query/find.rs: `--files` flag (doc: `Rank the repo's files for this text instead of matching node names: ids in the text first (through the repo's task / requirement rows and trackers), then past commits whose messages match it`); conflicts with `--kind`, `--no-collapse`, `--scope`; with `--with` the engine Err -> `error: ...` exit 2. Text output: `# files for `<query>``, the routed ids table when any (`| id | namespace | tier | route | defined at | state |`), then `| # | file | idr | text | ids |`; `--json` = the Answer envelope `{results, absence}`; exit 0 with rows, 1 on the absence (as find does today). Regenerate cli/surface/find.txt; README `glia find` usage line from it.
3. py/src/find.rs: `#[pyo3(signature = (query, top_k=20))] fn find_files(&self, ..)` on PyGraph using its `repo_roots`; returns the Answer as a native dict (LD.2); the engine Err is a `ValueError`. Regenerate py/api_surface/find.txt; test_find.py pins the method and the dict keys.
4. Marker: `[find-files] repo=<label> surface=<cli|py|lib> fusion=LX[IDR,T1s] ids=<n> idr_files=<i> text=<present|absent> text_files=<t> rows=<r>` plus the [intent] text / [idr] lines with the same surface.
Tests (engine/tests/find_files.rs, a scratch git repo with a history snapshot written through code-domain `write_history_with_messages` and a spec-kit task): `find_files("T012 export")` ranks the T012-named file first, then text matches; a query with no id and a matching past subject ranks that commit's files by BM25; ties broken by degree then path; no snapshot and no id -> absence naming both causes; two repos -> Err; identical answers across two builds.

packets.title: rank_eval parity rows for the ported intent mechanisms: `--engine on` recomputes T1s, IDR and the LX[IDR,H9s50] / LX[IDR,T1s] fusions through glia_engine::intent + algo::fuse from an in-memory snapshot, reports the mismatch count against the harness rankers, and feeds the gate; glia's own `.glia/overlay.toml [ids]` names its packet trackers
packets.area: EB measurement: engine-backed rankers in the gate
packets.rationale: Every ranking change must hold the gate: no recall@10 / MRR drop beyond CI on the fixed snapshots. The gate measures rank_eval's rankers; without engine-backed rows it cannot see a porting error in EB.3 / EB.6 / EB.2 (rename folding, the 4096-char body cap, the tracker reader replacing glia's lineage + LANDED-wave model). The BM25 arithmetic is deterministic, so fed the harness's own raw messages it must match T1s exactly; the stored messages are cleaned (trailer block, 4096-char cap, redaction), so that variant is a CI contrast, not an exact match; IDR's engine port is a different reader on glia, so it is reported with a CI, not a mismatch count.
entry_points: engine/examples/rank_eval.rs (new `--engine on` flag and its rows)
.glia/overlay.toml (new: glia's `[ids]`)
new files (new): .glia/overlay.toml
packets.implementation:
1. rank_eval `--engine on` (requires `--round1 on --round2 on`): for each test commit, the strictly older commits it already indexes become engine inputs. ENG-T1s-raw: `intent::text::TextIndex::from_docs` over the harness's own (sha, raw `%B` message, candidate indices) docs, then `scores(subject)`: the BM25 arithmetic, tokenizer and pooling must equal rank_eval's T1s bit for bit (mismatch = any query whose 20 top files or their scores differ). ENG-T1s: the same docs passed through code-domain `clean_message` first (what `history sync` stores): reported as a ranker with a recall@10 / MRR contrast against T1s and its CI. ENG-IDR: `intent::idr::route(subject, ..)` at the test commit's parent with `read_defs(Tree::Rev { parent }, &[], vocab, None)`, the repo's `IdVocab` read from the overlay at that parent (none -> defaults), `PathResolver` over the harness candidates and the renames `git_renames` already reads, recent = `recent_scopes` over the earlier test commits' subjects; `Candidates` are built from `g.paths` / `g.file_deg` through `Candidates::from_parts` (pub, #[doc(hidden)]). Fusions through `glia_activation::algo::fuse`: ENG-LX[IDR,P1] and ENG-LX[IDR,H9s50] (single and review shapes; P1 / T1s the harness's own vectors, so a difference isolates IDR) and ENG-LX[IDR,T1s] (find shape). They are pushed as ordinary rankers after every existing one, so no earlier row moves. Per repo: `[rank-eval] engine parity repo=<label> t1s_raw_mismatch=<q>/<n> t1s_clean_r10=<x> t1s_r10=<y> idr_r10=<a> harness_idr_r10=<b> routes=<route:n,..>` and a `### Engine parity` table in the round-1 md. Kina specifics stay in the private config the harness reads (no repo vocabulary in this file: the engine reads the repo's own `[ids]`).
2. .glia/overlay.toml (glia's own, checked in: .gitignore ignores only `.glia/graph/` and the snapshot dirs; version 2): `[ids] patterns = ["{U}.{N}{l?}"]` and two `[[ids.tracker]]` entries, `path = "dev-notes/leap-*-packets.json"` and `path = "dev-notes/leap-packets.json"`, each with `list = "packets"`, `files = "files_touched"` (no `state`: the packet files carry none; the harness's LANDED-wave state is open question 4). Check that `glia build .` prints the same `[overlay]` section counts apart from `ids=1`.
3. dev-notes/ranking-scoreboard.md: one row recording the parity run (aggregate numbers only for private repos).

INTEGRATOR NOTE (0.5.3 merge): file space: `Candidates::from_parts` is dropped; the harness builds `rank::FileIndex::of(&merged, ..)` (EA.9 already asserts it equals `g.paths`) and `Candidates::of(&fi, repo)`. Ordering: lands after EA.9 (same file; EA.9's prefix-count plumbing is reused for ENG-T1s' leak-free corpus). commons-lang / commons-io are not gate snapshots (the scope names glia + shell / websocket / samples): this packet's acceptance clones them itself, bare, under $HOME/.cache/glia-EB.9/, at round 3's revisions (apache/commons-lang `cee7cc6b`, apache/commons-io `11f0abe7`, dev-notes/ranking-eval-round3-2026-10-19.md line 8), and runs them with the same flags as scripts/rank-gate.sh (`--pick base,d85` included). Gate coverage for the intent answers (ANS:review, ANS:find_files, items 3 / 6 / 7) is EG.7's; this packet's ENG-* rows are parity, not gated.
packets.acceptance: cargo build --release --example rank_eval with zero warnings; on the public gate snapshots (the gate packet's list: glia, pop-os/shell, gorilla/websocket, flutter/samples, plus apache/commons-lang and apache/commons-io cloned by this packet at round 3's revisions, see the implementation's integrator note): `--round1 on --round2 on --engine on` prints `t1s_raw_mismatch=0/<n>` on every repo (exact: same tokenizer, BM25 float order and pooling); `ENG-T1s - T1s` recall@10 CI includes 0 or is above it on every repo (the cleaned, capped, redacted messages cost nothing measurable), else report blocked with the per-repo contrast; on repos with no `[ids]` and no conventional-commit scopes ENG-IDR is all zero and ENG-LX[IDR,P1] equals P1 exactly; on glia `ENG-LX[IDR,H9s50] - LX[IDR,H9s50]` recall@10 CI includes 0 or is above it (if below, report blocked with the per-route counts rather than tuning); every pre-existing ranker row reproduces exactly (0 differing values against the gate's stored baseline JSON). The gate (rank_eval-gate) passes with the ENG-* rows added to its checked list.

packets.implementation:
All in engine/src/calibrate/record.rs (new) unless named. engine/src/calibrate/mod.rs is the E0 slot's directory-module file; this packet adds only `pub mod record;` and `pub use record::{..}` there (never engine/src/lib.rs).

1. Layout: `<root>/.glia/calibration-snapshot/calibration.json` and `meta.json` (written LAST). `.glia` via glia_code_domain::walk_gating::CONTROL_DIR.

2. Types (serde Serialize + Deserialize, #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)], #[non_exhaustive], fields pub):
- CalibrationMeta { version, generator, build_stamp (glia_stamp::BUILD_STAMP at write time), ranker_revision, history_head (HistoryMeta.head of the snapshot replayed), history_data_hash (HistoryMeta.data_hash), messages_hash: Option<String> (EB.1's HistoryMeta.messages_hash, None when the snapshot had no messages), sets: usize, data_hash }. CalibrationMeta::new(head, data_hash, messages_hash) fills the constants; write_calibration fills sets and data_hash.
- Calibration { replay: ReplayParamsRecord, sets: Vec<CalibratedSet> } sorted by (set asc, shape order k1 < k2 < k3 < half < find).
- ReplayParamsRecord { max_commits, max_seeds, max_files, commits, train_commits, test_commits }.
- CalibratedSet { set: String, shape: String, candidates: Vec<String> (selection order), digest, fallback: String, test_commits (with >= 1 query of this shape), queries, recall10: Vec<f64> and mrr: Vec<f64> (per candidate, summed over queries), fallback_recall10: f64, fallback_mrr: f64 (summed), pick: String (the online rule's next step: argmax of the summed recall@10 over every replayed query, ties to the earlier candidate), last_online_pick: String (the pick the rule made AT the newest test commit, i.e. before that commit's queries were added: rank_eval's `pick_at_the_last_test_commit`), online: OnlineReplay }.
- OnlineReplay { selection_recall10, fallback_recall10, selection_mrr, fallback_mrr (means over queries), picks: BTreeMap<String, usize> (test commits per online pick, rank_eval's `picks_per_test_commit`), per_commit: Vec<CommitScore> }; CommitScore { queries: u32, sel_r10, fb_r10, sel_mrr, fb_mrr } (sums over that test commit's queries; the unit EC.5's commit-cluster bootstrap resamples).
f64s as serde_json writes them (shortest round-trip, deterministic); sums of values in [0, 1], an empty set writes 0.0, never NaN.

3. set_digest(candidates) = glia_code_domain::snapshots::data_hash(&[format!("rev={RANKER_REVISION}\n").as_bytes(), candidates.join("\n").as_bytes()]).

4. write_calibration: create the dir; remove an existing meta.json first (a write stopped part-way leaves a record the reader rejects); calibration.json = serde_json::to_vec_pretty + trailing newline, written atomically (temp file in the dir + rename: copy code-domain/src/snapshots.rs `write_atomic`, which is private there); meta.sets / meta.data_hash = data_hash(&[&bytes]); meta.json atomically. Marker `[calibration] wrote dir=<dir> sets=<n> build_stamp=<s> history_head=<12 hex>`.

5. read_calibration(root): no dir -> Absent; meta.json missing / unparsable -> Rejected("incomplete"); version != CALIBRATION_VERSION -> Rejected("version"); calibration.json missing, hash != meta.data_hash, unparsable or sets count != meta.sets -> Rejected("incomplete"); build_stamp != glia_stamp::BUILD_STAMP -> Rejected("build_stamp") (strict: the graph the replay ranked over may have moved; open question 2); ranker_revision != RANKER_REVISION -> Rejected("ranker_revision"); else Loaded. One line per call: `[calibration] read root=<root> status=loaded|absent|rejected reason=<r|-> sets=<n> history_head=<12 hex|->`.

6. load_for_roots(roots): 0 roots -> NotLoaded; > 1 -> Rejected("multi_repo") (a calibration is per repo; a `--with` merge answers on the fallback, open question 4); 1 -> read_calibration(Path::new(root)).

7. Shape::from_seed_files(n): 0 | 1 -> K1, 2 -> K2, 3 -> K3, _ -> Half (the replay's shapes: one seed file; two; three; half of a 4+ file change). Find is set explicitly. as_str k1 k2 k3 half find; order() -> u8 for sorting.

8. select(read, set, shape, candidates, fallback) -> Selection { set, shape, pick, source: "calibrated" | "fallback", reason: Option<&'static str>, test_commits }: NotLoaded -> fallback `not_loaded`; Absent -> `absent`; Rejected(r) -> r; Loaded with no row of (set, shape) -> `no_set`; row digest != set_digest(candidates) or pick not in candidates -> `candidate_set`; row queries == 0 -> `no_queries`; else the row's pick, source calibrated, reason None. The caller always names the fallback (the surface's uncalibrated ranking); select never invents one. explicit(set, shape, name) is the Selection of a ranking the caller chose by flag: source "explicit", reason None (EC.8 / EC.9 report it so `[select]` always fires once per answer).

9. log_selection(surface, s): `[select] surface=<surface> set=<set> shape=<shape> pick=<pick> source=<calibrated|fallback|explicit> reason=<r|-> test_commits=<n>`.

10. engine/src/watch.rs `durability`: inside the CONTROL_DIR branch, `rest == "calibration-snapshot" || rest.starts_with("calibration-snapshot/")` returns Durability::Low, as `graph` does; one row added to `durability_table`.

11. engine/tests/calibrate_record.rs (new): round trip (write then read is Loaded and equal); meta removed -> Rejected(incomplete); calibration.json edited by one byte -> Rejected(incomplete); meta.build_stamp rewritten -> Rejected(build_stamp); version 2 -> Rejected(version); ranker_revision 0 -> Rejected(ranker_revision); select() for each reason (not_loaded, absent, no_set, candidate_set by digest, candidate_set by pick, no_queries, calibrated) and explicit(); from_seed_files 0..6; load_for_roots with two roots -> Rejected(multi_repo); two writes of one Calibration are byte-identical.

INTEGRATOR NOTE (0.5.3 merge): `CommitScore` gains `pub sha: String` and `pub pick: String` (the online pick the rule made AT that test commit, from strictly earlier test commits only), so a caller can replay the online selection commit by commit (EG.6 / EG.7 feed each gate query its own commit's pick: leak-free by the online rule). The record grows by one short string pair per (set, shape, test commit).

packets.implementation:
engine/src/calibrate/replay.rs (new), `pub mod replay;` in engine/src/calibrate/mod.rs.

1. File space: EB.3's `Candidates` (paths sorted, `position(path)`, `deg`). A path the candidates lack is dropped from a commit.

2. build_replay(snapshot, messages, cands, params, shapes):
- `crate::external::commit_file_sets(snapshot)` (newest first, current paths), zipped with snapshot.commits and, when present, EB.1's `HistoryMessage` rows (same order, same shas: read_history_messages checks it); files mapped through cands.position, sorted, deduped; subject = the message's `s`, message = `s` + "\n" + `b` (EB.3's doc text, so replay and answer index the same text); no sidecar -> both empty and Replay.messages = false. Reverse to oldest first.
- train[k] = 1 <= files.len() <= max_files; test-eligible = 2 <= files.len() <= max_files; tests = the last `max_commits` test-eligible indices, oldest first.
- Queries are built DURING a forward pass with a CoState so each query's C0 is read before its commit is observed: for k in 0..n: if k is a test commit (ordinal tc): ord = its files sorted by seed_order_hash(sha, path) (stable, ties keep file order); K1: for s in ord[..min(max_seeds, n)]: seeds [s], weights [1.0], targets = files without s in file order, c0 = c0_seeds(&[s]); K2 (n >= 3): seeds ord[..2], targets ord[2..]; K3 (n >= 4): ord[..3] / ord[3..]; Half (n >= 4): ord[..n/2] / ord[n/2..] (c0 = c0_seeds(seeds)); Find: built later by EC.3's driver (its seeds need the text ranking), recorded here as a placeholder query with seeds [] and targets = files in file order. Then, if train[k], co.observe(files). Only the requested shapes are built; order (tc, shape order, seed order).
- CoState::observe: cnt[a] += 1 per file; co[a][b] += 1 for each ordered pair a != b (rank_eval's loop). c0_seeds: per seed s, d = cnt[s] + 1, acc[f] += co[s][f] / d in (seed order, f asc) into a BTreeMap (r3_tqueries' accumulation order; k1's one seed is run_query's `c0`). c0_weighted(top): tot = sum of weights; acc[f] += w / tot * co[g][f] / (cnt[g] + 1) in (top order, f asc). seed_order_hash: copy rank_eval.rs `h64` and `mix` exactly (FNV offset 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325, prime 0x0100_0000_01b3; z ^= z >> 30; z *= 0xbf58_476d_1ce4_e5b9; z ^= z >> 27; z *= 0x94d0_49bb_1331_11eb; z ^= z >> 31). find_top(t1s): entries > 0.0, sorted by (score desc total_cmp, index asc), truncated to 10, weights score / total.
- One marker: `[calibrate] replay commits=<c> train=<t> test_eligible=<e> test=<n> messages=<yes|no> queries k1=<a> k2=<b> k3=<c> half=<d> find=<f>`.

3. The driver (EC.3) replays the same forward pass for the rankers' own state (CoState again for the find shape's C0x, EC.4's text corpus, EC.10's work state), always scoring a test commit before observing it.

4. Unit tests (#[cfg(test)], a synthetic HistorySnapshot as engine/tests/cochange.rs builds one, no git): eligibility (a 1-file commit trains but is no test; a 31-file commit is neither); max_commits keeps the newest; k1 seeds follow the hash order and stop at max_seeds; k2 / k3 / half need 3 / 4 / 4 files and keep hash-ordered targets; a renamed file's old path maps to its current candidate; C0 of a test commit excludes that commit's own pairs (leak test) and equals hand counts; seed_order_hash("abc", "src/a.rs") equals a literal computed once with rank_eval.rs's h64 and written into the test; c0_weighted on a hand case; no messages sidecar -> messages=no and empty subjects.

EC's verifier's tolerance for `the rename fold` and `EB.3's generated-file rule` is therefore gone: the replay's file space and C0 are the answer's. CoState implements EA.3's `rank::CochangeHistory` (count / cochanged as sorted (file, n) slices: keep `co` as a Vec<Vec<(u32, u32)>> updated by binary-search insert, never a HashMap), and `c0_seeds(seeds)` returns exactly `rank::c0(self, seeds, n)` (the dense form; the sparse (file, c0) list is derived from it), so the replay and the answer share EA.3's one C0 loop; a unit test asserts it. The parity test in step 4 `a renamed file's old path maps to its current candidate` is replaced by `a pre-rename commit's old path drops` (EA.3's rename test, 2/5 not 4/5).

packets.title: Replay evaluation and the online pick: the Candidate trait (rank from the prefix state, observe after scoring), a per-query Memo, rank_eval's eval_ex (seeds excluded, ties to the smaller file index), recall@10 / MRR, and r3_select's prequential rule (best summed recall@10 over earlier test commits of that shape, ties to the earlier candidate, commits with no query skipped) per (set, shape) into CalibratedSet rows
packets.area: EC item 4: the driver that turns a Replay and candidate sets into calibration rows (engine/src/calibrate/candidate.rs, engine/src/calibrate/select.rs)
packets.rationale:
The selection rule is the measured one verbatim (rank_eval.rs `r3_select`, `round1_select`): per test commit WITH queries of the shape (r3_select skips the rest: `if qs.is_empty() { continue }`), the candidate with the best SUMMED recall@10 over every earlier query of that shape; candidate 0 before any (`seen == 0`); ties to the earlier candidate (`max_by(.. .then(b.cmp(&a)))`); then that commit's queries are added. The pick the answers use is the rule's next step (argmax over all replayed queries); the record also keeps the pick AT the newest test commit, which is what rank_eval prints, so EC.5's parity check compares like with like.
Metrics are rank_eval.rs `eval_ex`: a target's rank = 1 + the non-excluded files other than it whose key is better (`better`: lexicographic on [f64; 3], then the smaller index); recall@10 = share of targets ranked <= 10; MRR = 1 / best rank. Seeds are excluded in seeded shapes, nothing in find.
Candidates share expensive signals (one PPR per damping per query, one BM25 per commit), so the driver gives each query one Memo.

packets.implementation:
1. candidate.rs: the types above. RankKey is rank_eval's `Key` (descending lexicographic; a scalar score s is [s, 0, 0]; LX[a, b, c] is [a, b, c]). rank() returns exactly cands.paths.len() keys (debug_assert; release: a short vector is an Err row the driver reports as `[calibrate] candidate <name> returned <n> keys of <m>` and the set is not written).

2. select.rs: `better` copied from rank_eval.rs; eval_query(keys, excluded, targets): per target t, rank = 1 + |{f : !excluded[f] && f != t && better(keys[f], f, keys[t], t)}|; ranks sorted; recall@10 = |{r <= 10}| / |targets|; MRR = 1 / ranks[0]. A query with no target is never built.

3. run_sets(merged, cands, root, replay, state, specs):
- A spec whose fallback is not one of its candidates carries `fallback_candidate` (scored, never selectable).
- Walk replay.commits oldest first. At a test commit: (a) the find queries of this commit get their seeds / weights / C0x now (state's text corpus scores the subject; replay::find_top; CoState::c0_weighted), (b) its queries are scored with crate::parallel::par_map_ordered (order-preserving): per query one Memo, excluded = seeds unless Find, then for each spec whose shapes include the query's shape, for each candidate (and fallback) keys = rank(..) and eval_query; (c) sequentially in query order the results fold into accumulators. THEN state.observe(commit, train[k]) (every commit, test or not; the prefix state never sees a commit before its queries are scored).
- Accumulator per (spec, shape): sum_r10[c], sum_mrr[c], fallback sums, queries, test_commits, per_commit: Vec<CommitScore>, picks. For a test commit with >= 1 query of the shape: best = if queries == 0 {0} else argmax_c sum_r10[c], ties to the smaller c; record last_online_pick = name(best); picks[name(best)] += 1; its queries add sel / fb recall@10 and MRR into a CommitScore; then their candidate values add into sum_r10 / sum_mrr. Commits with no query of the shape touch nothing.
- Rows: one CalibratedSet per (spec, shape) (0 queries -> pick = candidates[0], queries 0, so select() answers `no_queries`); candidates = names in order; digest = set_digest(names); pick = argmax over all sums (ties to the earlier); online means = sums / queries. One line per row (fired_on_marker).
- Every f64 sum folds in query order on one thread: the record is byte-identical at any GLIA_THREADS.

4. Unit tests (select.rs #[cfg(test)]): eval_query on a hand case (ties to the smaller index; excluded seeds do not count); the online rule over three scripted test candidates reproduces a hand-computed pick sequence, including a tie (earlier wins), the first commit (candidate 0) and a commit with no query of the shape (skipped: no pick counted, as r3_select); last_online_pick vs pick differ on a script where the newest commit flips the argmax; leak: a candidate that ranks by state's observed-commit count sees k at commit k's queries; the fallback candidate is never a pick.

INTEGRATOR NOTE (0.5.3 merge): run_sets fills CommitScore.sha / .pick (EC.1's integrator note) for every test commit with a query of the shape.

packets.title: The structure bank and its two sets (item 10 with item 2): the replay's file rankers P1, PT*, B0, H10, H10[PT*], H10[B0] ported from rank_eval run_query / bfs_key / file_pool (undirected PPR over every node of each file, max vs sum pooling, carry BFS Walk::Both) on EA.1's PprIndex; SELs0 = {P1, PT*, B0} (fallback P1) and SELh0 = {H10, H10[PT*], H10[B0]} (fallback H10) on k1 / k2 / k3 / half
packets.area: EC item 10: the text-free answers' candidate sets and the replay rankers they score (engine/src/calibrate/bank.rs, engine/src/calibrate/sets.rs)
packets.rationale:
Item 10 (confirmed 2026-10-23): 'structure-only selection for the answers with no text: item 4's online pick over {PPR, PPR d0.85 + sum, BFS}, calibrated on the answer's own shape'. Item 2 (agreed) makes co-change the tie-break in impact / review / pack, and EA.2 / EA.5 make it the answers' default (Ranking::default() = co-change first, PPR: rank_eval's H10). round 3's D2 table (ranking-eval-round3-2026-10-19-tables.md) measured both readings on 12 repos, single seed: SELs0 = online pick of {P1, PT*, B0}, never below P1, CI above 0 on 7; SELh0 = online pick of {H10, H10[PT*], H10[B0]}: H10 is far above every structure-only ranker (glia 0.321 vs SELs0 0.299, shell 0.738 vs 0.676, commons-lang 0.579 vs 0.460), and SELh0 - H10 is above 0 on two private repos (+0.014, +0.026), n.s. elsewhere. Applying a SELs0 pick to an answer that is co-change first by default would DROP co-change and lose up to 0.12 recall@10 on calibrated repos. So both sets are calibrated: the answer reads SELh0 when its ranking is co-change first (the default) and SELs0 when the caller turned co-change off (`--no-cochange`, cochange=False). Both are item 10's three bases; SELh0 puts item 2's co-change in front of each.
The bank ports the measured rankers, not the answers' presentation: rank_eval pools node scores over EVERY node of a file and runs PPR undirected with top_k unbounded (`undirected(None, Direction::Undirected)`, top_k usize::MAX); B0 is reach::bfs over Adjacency::carry, Walk::Both, unbounded depth, key [-min depth (unreached -1e9), file degree, 0] (`bfs_key`); P1 = damping CODE_TABLES' own (0.5), max pool; PT* = damping 0.85 with the base weights, sum pool (round-1 Q4: `--pick base,d85`); H10[X] = LX[C0, X] (`lex2(c0, x)`; H10[B0] = [c0, -depth, deg]).

packets.implementation:
1. bank.rs StructIndex::build(merged, cands): file_nodes[f] = the nodes located in candidate file f (one Locator; the same MODULE-file membership EB.3 uses), in node order; p05 / p85 = EA.1 `PprIndex::build(&merged node ids, all edges, &cfg)` with cfg = CODE_TABLES.activation_config(None), cfg.direction = Direction::Undirected, cfg.top_k = usize::MAX (p85: cfg.damping = 0.85, rank::WIDE_DAMPING); carry = Adjacency::carry(merged, &CODE_TABLES). Built once per calibrate run, held by ReplayState.

2. Seeds: uniform_seed_nodes(seed files) = every node of every seed file, weight 1 / count (rank_eval Ppr::uniform over the flattened file_nodes); weighted_seed_nodes(top) = for each (file, w): w / |nodes| per node (r3_transfer's find rule). ppr_files runs the index with that personalisation (EA.1's weighted entry: see risks) and pools per file: max (P1) or sum (PT*) of the node scores, summed in node order (rank_eval file_pool). Empty personalisation -> all zeros. bfs_files: glia_activation::algo::reach::bfs(&carry, seeds, Walk::Both, usize::MAX), min depth per file, key [-depth or -1e9, deg[f], 0.0] with deg = EB.3 Candidates.deg (rank_eval file_deg: the sum of every edge endpoint on the file's nodes).

3. structure_keys(name, q): seeds = q.query.seeds (file indices); p1 = memo "p1" ppr_files(uniform, 0.5, max), pt = memo "pt" (0.85, sum), b0 = memo "b0" bfs_files, c0 = dense from q.query.c0 (EC.2). P1 -> scalar(p1); PT* -> scalar(pt); B0 -> b0; H10 -> [c0, p1, 0]; H10[PT*] -> [c0, pt, 0]; H10[B0] -> [c0, b0[0], b0[1]]. Any other name -> None.

4. sets.rs: specs(groups) returns the SetSpecs of the named groups in registration order; this packet registers group "structure" = [SetSpec { SELh0, SEEDED_SHAPES, fallback H10, Named over COCHANGE_CANDIDATES }, SetSpec { SELs0, SEEDED_SHAPES, fallback P1, Named over STRUCTURE_CANDIDATES }]; an unknown group is Err naming the known ones. EC.11 / EC.13 append "review" / "find".

5. Pin tests (sets.rs #[cfg(test)]): both candidate lists, their order and set_digest values are literals, so a rename or reorder fails until RANKER_REVISION is bumped with the literal. A bank test on a 6-node toy graph: H10's keys equal [c0, p1, 0] with ties to the smaller path; B0's unreached file is -1e9; PT* sums where P1 takes the max.

INTEGRATOR NOTE (0.5.3 merge): rebound to EA's final API (EA's verifier changed what EC.4 was drafted against). StructIndex holds no PPR index or adjacency of its own: it holds one `Arc<rank::RankCache>` (EA.2) built over the merged graph with the repo root, whose `ppr_index` / `carry` / `files` serve every query, and the per-file keys come from EA.4: `ppr_files` / `bfs_files` are `rank::base_keys(merged, &cache, pers, RankBase::{Ppr | PprWide | Bfs})` (pers = `uniform_seed_nodes` or `weighted_seed_nodes`), and H10 / H10[PT*] / H10[B0] are `rank::rank_files_with_c0(.., Ranking::from_harness_name(name), Some(&dense_c0))` keys, dense_c0 = the query's prefix C0 from EC.2 (EA.4's integrator note). So the replay scores the arithmetic the answers run (EA.9 proves that arithmetic equals rank_eval's P1 / PT* / B0 / H10 / H10[PT*] / H10[B0] in f64 bits). The weighted personalisation the risks ask for is EA.1's `vector_weighted` (added to EA.1 at integration). The risk paragraph's `the answers pool over their own universe` no longer holds: EA.4's rank_files ranks every candidate file exactly as here; only the ROW presentation (EA.4 order_rows) is the answer's own. ONE file space (integration): every `Candidates` / `cands` in this packet is EB.3's per-repo view over EA.3's `glia_engine::rank::FileIndex` (rank_eval's index_graph rule, generated MODULE files dropped exactly as the harness drops them), and commit files map through `HistoryFile.p` with NO rename fold (EA.3 / the harness's `--no-renames`): `external::commit_file_sets` is not called. EC's verifier's tolerance for `the rename fold` and `EB.3's generated-file rule` is therefore gone: the replay's file space and C0 are the answer's.

packets.risks: needs EA.1: a weighted personalisation entry on PprIndex (`vector_weighted(&[(NodeId, f64)])`, ppr_vector's tail with the given weights instead of 1 / seed_count): the find shape personalises over the text's top files by score (r3_transfer), and EA.1 as drafted takes uniform seeds only; the integrator adds it to EA.1 (or EC.4 adds it to activation/src/ppr_index.rs after EA.1 lands). The bank and the answers differ by design: the answers (EA.4 / EA.5) pool over their own universe (blast closure within depth, pack's reached nodes) and their PPR follows the blast plan's direction; the replay scores rank_eval's rankers, which is what the selections were measured on. The calibration therefore picks a BASE (ppr / ppr-wide / bfs, co-change first or not) and the answer applies that base its own way; EG.1's ANS rankers measure the answers. packets.title: The calibration step: `calibrate::calibrate(root, merged, opts)` reads the history snapshot and its messages, replays them, writes the record and returns a summary with each row's online selection - fallback recall@10 and a commit-cluster bootstrap CI; parity with rank_eval on a public snapshot

packets.rationale: Item 4 puts the replay 'in the snapshot step', 'a new step beside history sync': it runs git-free over `.glia/history-snapshot/` (with EB.1's messages.jsonl) against the graph of the layout and writes `.glia/calibration-snapshot/`; a build never runs it and the answers only read its record. packets.title: Calibrated selection in blast_radius, diff_impact and review's impact (item 10 with item 2): the record held by EA's RankCache; inside `radius`, the shape from the seeds' distinct files and select(SELh0 when the ranking is co-change first, SELs0 when not) replaces BlastOptions.ranking unless the caller chose a ranking explicitly; `selection` on BlastRadius; CLI / pyo3 `--ranking` / `ranking=` become optional
packets.area: EC item 10: the text-free blast-radius family reads the calibration (engine/src/answers.rs, engine/src/rank/cache.rs, CLI blast-radius / diff-impact / review, pyo3 blast / diff_impact / review)
packets.rationale:
Item 10 names blast_radius, impact and pack. diff_impact's `impact` is a BlastRadius (engine/src/diff_impact.rs, through blast_radius_seeded) and review's impact list is diff_impact_from_delta's, so the pick enters in one place: `radius` in engine/src/answers.rs, where the seeds are resolved and located (the shape needs the seeds' distinct files). The CLI `glia impact` (cli/src/cmd/impact.rs) is an unranked depth table and is not touched.
Where the record comes from: EA.2's RankCache already holds the repo roots and lives exactly as long as the graph it serves (PyGraph, WatchSession, one CLI command; a transient one in diff_impact_from_delta). It loads the record once, as it loads the co-change index (EA.3), so no answer re-reads a file per call and a library caller with no cache answers exactly as EA left it.
Which set: EA's default Ranking is co-change first (item 2); the calibration offers SELh0 (H10 / H10[PT*] / H10[B0], fallback H10 = EA's default) for it, and SELs0 (P1 / PT* / B0, fallback P1) when the caller turned co-change off. An explicit `--ranking` (or pyo3 `ranking=`) is the user's choice and is never overridden. With no record, every answer is byte-identical to EA's.

1. RankCache::calibration(): OnceLock::get_or_init(|| CalibrationHandle::new(load_for_roots(&self.roots))); empty roots -> NotLoaded. guard() replaces the OnceLock (a new graph shape re-reads the record).
2. radius(): when ids is non-empty: seed files = loc.locate(id).file for each seed (Some only), distinct; n = count. If opts.select is false or no rank_cache: sel = explicit(set, shape, opts.ranking.harness_name()) and the ranking stays. Else sel = select(..) as in entry_points; ranking = Ranking::from_harness_name(&sel.pick) (always Some: every candidate and fallback name maps; a None is a bug, debug_assert, and release keeps opts.ranking). The effective ranking feeds EA.5's ranking step unchanged (EA owns the ordering; this packet only chooses the Ranking). BlastRadius.selection = Some(sel); no seed -> None. packets.area: EC item 4: work neighbourhood and milestone signals (engine/src/calibrate/work.rs)
packets.rationale:
6 of SELt's 10 candidates (HTsa/HTsc/HTsd[W5], HTsc/HTsd[M], ALL5) and ALL5x in find's SELf2t read W5 and M, and no other group ports them (EA ports structure and co-change, EB text and ids). Without them the measured sets cannot be built; round 1's SELt0 (no W / M) measured within ±0.01 of SELt, but SELt2 / SELf2t without them were never measured as sets, and ALL5x is find's most frequent pick (7 of 12 repos). So EC owns them, ported from rank_eval.rs `R1State` (round 1):
- W_k (r1_window): over the training commits so far, the j-th newest (j = 1) weighs R1_DECAY^(j-1), 0.75; W5 = k 5;
- M (R1State::test): Mid (labels from a repo's own plan ids: rank_eval's `--pre` modes, repo-specific) else Mbr (the test commit's merged-branch label: lab_files of `br:<label>`) else Mgap (the test commit joins the current segment when its author time is within R1_GAP_S, 24 h, of the newest training commit; segments split when a training commit is more than 24 h after the previous one or shares no file with the segment's last R1_OVERLAP_LAST, 3, commits) else empty. On the public repos the measured M was Mbr / Mgap; Mid is repo-specific and is not ported (no repo's plan vocabulary enters the engine).
Mbr and Mgap read author time and the merged-branch label, which the history snapshot does not hold (commits.jsonl has committer time and no merges): EB.1's messages sidecar must carry them (risks).

The replay uses each test commit's own subject as that title, over the full messages of strictly older commits (rank_eval `bm`).
Definitions (rank_eval.rs r3_bank_seed, round1_rankers; mm = min-max over the non-excluded files, a flat vector 0): H9s50 = 0.5 mm(T1s) + 0.5 mm(P1); H9s25[PT*] = 0.25 mm(T1s) + 0.75 mm(PT*); H18s[PT*] = mean(mm(T1s), mm(C0), mm(PT*)); H10[PT*] = [C0, PT*]; HTs{tag}[W5] = a mm(T1s) + b mm(W5) + c mm(P1) with HT_GRID a (0.5, 0.25, 0.25), c (0.25, 0.25, 0.5), d (1/3 each); HTs{tag}[M] the same with M; ALL5 = mean(mm(T1s), mm(W5), mm(M), mm(C0), mm(P1)).
One code path: the replay must measure what the answer does, so review's intent ranking is computed by the same bank functions at answer time (signals over the whole candidate set: P1 / PT* from the changed files' nodes, C0 from EA.3's index, T1s from EB.3's index, W5 / M from EC.10), and EB.7's fixed LX[IDR,H9s50] becomes the fallback the bank also computes.

Definitions (r3_bank_find; mm over every file, nothing excluded): the text's top 10 positive files (score desc, then index) with weights score / total personalise PX1 (damping 0.5, max pool) and PXT (0.85, sum) and weight C0x; H9x = 0.5 mm(T1s) + 0.5 mm(PX1); H9x25T = 0.25 mm(T1s) + 0.75 mm(PXT); H18x = mean(mm(T1s), mm(C0x), mm(PXT)); H10x = [C0x, PXT]; ALL5x = mean(mm(T1s), mm(W5), mm(M), mm(C0x), mm(PXT)); LX[IDR,H18x], LX[IDR,H9x25T], H18xi = mean(mm(IDR), mm(T1s), mm(C0x), mm(PXT)), LX[IDR,C0x,PXT]. packets.rationale: The 0.5.3 gate (next-leap-0.5.3.md, Gate: 'rank_eval runs as a release check on fixed repo snapshots ... A ranking change that lowers recall@10 or MRR beyond its CI fails the close-out') must measure what consumers get. At HEAD b3fc2ac7 every ranker in engine/examples/rank_eval.rs is harness code (P1, PT*, B0, H10, H9s50, LX[IDR,..], SELt2, SELs0, SELf2t ...): none calls an engine answer, so porting items 1-11 into blast_radius / diff_impact / review / pack / find would move nothing the harness reports. Its `impact` is LD.5's multi-seed blast radius, the impact section review reports), the pack answer through `glia_engine::pack::pack_ids`, and the find answer through `glia_engine::find::find_nodes` on the commit subject. Second, the harness's reference rankers read `CODE_TABLES.activation_config(..)` on top of `ActivationConfig::default()` (activation/src/lib.rs: damping 0.5, max_iterations 100, epsilon 1e-6), so a 0.5.3 packet that changes a default would silently move the reference P1 the gate compares against; the reference must be pinned.
