Prerequisite: the Kina-scrub commit (Kina-domain constants moved out of rank_eval.rs into the private `~/Code/kina-extras/` config, next-leap-0.5.3.md Order 1) has landed; build on it and keep every addition domain-free (no Kina names, law or spec text).
1. Reference pin. Add `const REF_DAMPING: f64 = 0.5; const REF_MAX_ITER: usize = 100; const REF_EPS: f64 = 1e-6;` (and `REF_SPECIFICITY = glia_activation::Specificity::None`, the 0.5.2 value activation/src/profile.rs's `activation_config_applies_weights_then_preset` test pins) with a doc comment ('the 0.5.2 PPR the reference rankers measure; pinned so an engine default change never moves the reference'). In the `undirected` closure and at each other `CODE_TABLES.activation_config(None)` site set `c.damping = REF_DAMPING; c.max_iterations = REF_MAX_ITER; c.epsilon = REF_EPS; c.node_specificity = REF_SPECIFICITY;` (the d85 variants that already set damping keep their own value: set the pin first, then their override). Edge weights stay CODE_TABLES' (a weight change is a graph-ranking change the gate is meant to see on ANS rankers; note it in the doc comment). At HEAD the values equal the defaults, so every existing ranker reproduces bit for bit.
2. ANS rankers. `rows_to_keys`: walk the answer's rows in the answer's rank order (blast / diff-impact `impact.results` and find `results` in vector order; pack `nodes` sorted by `PackedNode.rank` ascending, since the manifest's vector order is the render order, not the candidate order); the first row whose `file` maps to a candidate file index (a lookup map path -> index built once on Ctx as `path_ix: HashMap<String, u32>`, only ever looked up, never iterated) gives that file key `[-(k as f64), 0.0, 0.0]` where k is the order of first appearance (0, 1, ...); every file no row reaches gets `[f64::NEG_INFINITY; 3]` (the harness's tie rule then orders unreached files by path, as every other ranker's ties). `ans_keys_seed(ctx, seeds)`: text = the seed files' repo-relative paths joined by '\n' (diff_items' changed-file-list form: no `+++ ` line); `let d = glia_engine::diff_impact::diff_impact_from_diff(ctx.merged, &text, &BlastOptions::default());` keys from `d.impact.results` (`file` per row) -> ('ANS:impact', keys); `let seeds_ids` = every node of the seed files (`g.file_nodes` -> `g.ids`), `let p = glia_engine::pack::pack_ids(ctx.merged, &seed_ids, &PackArgs::default());` keys from `p.nodes` -> ('ANS:pack', keys). `ans_keys_find(ctx, subject)`: `let mut o = FindOptions::default(); o.top_k = 0;` `find_nodes(ctx.merged, subject, &o).results` -> ('ANS:find', keys). Use each type's Default and field assignment (they are #[non_exhaustive]); check the import paths with grep (`pub mod diff_impact`, `pub mod pack`, `pub mod find` in engine/src/lib.rs; BlastOptions is flat) and use exactly the public paths. Seed files are excluded by the harness's `excl` as for every seed ranker. Pooling: the ANS keys roll node rows up to files by first appearance (a max-style roll-up); none of the 0.5.2 answers exposes a file-level ranking (BlastAnswer / PackedNode / FoundNode are node rows). Contract for the porting groups, written into the doc comment on `rows_to_keys`: a packet that adds a file-level roll-up to an answer (item 1's sum pooling in blast radius / pack) switches that answer's ANS ranker to read the roll-up in the same packet. Expected at 0.5.2: ANS:find is near 0 (find's tiers match identifiers; a whole commit subject matches at most through `subsequence`); that is the consumer-visible answer items 3 / 6 / 11 change, recorded as is, never special-cased.
3. Wiring: when `args.ans == "on"`, run_query appends the two seed rankers after every existing bank entry (so existing ranker order and every selection's candidate positions are unchanged); r3_transfer gets `subjects: &[String]` (index by test commit: `subject(&commits[test_idx[tc]].msg).to_string()`, the string round 1's T1s query is built from) and an `ans: bool`; its k2 / k3 / half closure appends ANS:impact / ANS:pack (seeds = q.seeds), its find closure appends ANS:find. Append before the `eval_ex` loop so they are scored like every ranker.
4. `--r3-perq on` also writes `doc["perq_shapes"] = {<shape>: {"ids": [..], "commit_of": [..], "r10": {ranker: [..]}, "mrr": {ranker: [..]}}}` for every non-empty R3_SHAPES entry of `transfer`, where an id is `<test sha>:<shape>:<seed paths sorted, joined by '+'>` (find: `<test sha>:find`) and commit_of is the test commit index (the shape's `tc_of`); `perq` (single seed) is unchanged. Rankers per shape are `outs[0].names` (selections included, after r3_select ran).
5. Marker: once per run with --ans on, `eprintln!("[rank_eval] ans rankers={} single={} transfer={} find={} ms={}", ..)` (rankers added, queries scored per shape, wall ms of the ANS calls summed from Instant timers around them). packets.title: rank_eval `--gate-check`: per (repo, shape, gated ranker) paired recall@10 and MRR against a stored baseline with the commit-cluster bootstrap; a drop whose 95% CI lies wholly below 0 fails (exit 1), query drift exits 2; `--gate-trim` writes a baseline holding only the gated rankers
packets.area: EG rank_eval release gate: the fail rule
packets.rationale: The gate's fail rule must use the reports' own statistics: every contrast in the six reports is the paired commit-cluster bootstrap of rank_eval.rs `fn paired` (B = --boot, 95% percentile CI, fixed RNG seed 0x5eed_2026_1018), and `--r3-compare a.json,b.json` (fn r3_compare_main) already pairs two runs' per-query dumps but only renders a table: it neither selects rankers nor decides. A release check needs a verdict and an exit code, over the single-seed shape and the round-3 shapes EG.1 dumps, and a baseline small enough to commit (a full perq dump carries 400+ rankers).

packets.implementation:
gate.json (written by EG.3; read here) is `{"gate":1, "metrics":["r10","mrr"], "rankers": {"single": [..], "k2": [..], "k3": [..], "half": [..], "find": [..]}, "items": {..}}`; `items` is EG.3's coverage map, which rank_eval reads only to check that every ranker it names is also listed under `rankers` (else `[rank-gate] items name ungated ranker=<r>`, exit 2).
1. `--gate-trim <gate.json> --out <baseline.json> <run.json via --gate-new>`: read the run JSON (EG.1's `perq` and `perq_shapes`), keep per shape only `ids`, `commit_of` and the r10 / mrr arrays of the gate's rankers, plus `{"label", "rev"}` from `stats` and `"glia_head"` from env `GLIA_RANK_GATE_HEAD` (the engine commit that produced it; EG.3 sets it). A gated ranker missing from the run is an error: print `[rank-gate] missing ranker=<r> shape=<s> label=<l>` and exit 2. Write compact (`serde_json::to_string` over BTreeMaps, sorted keys, no pretty-printing: the baselines are committed and the ratchet rewrites them, so size matters), so the same run trims to the same bytes. Values are copied as the run's f64s, never rounded, so an unchanged ranker diffs exactly 0. The single-seed shape is stored under `single`.
2. `--gate-check <gate.json> --gate-base <baseline.json> --gate-new <run.json> --out <verdict.json> --md <verdict.md>`: for each shape in gate order, require `ids` equal between base and new (else print `[rank-gate] drift label=<l> shape=<s> base_queries=<a> new_queries=<b> common=<c>` and remember exit 2: the snapshot or the candidate-file set moved, and only a declared re-baseline fixes it); for each gated ranker and metric, `let p = paired(&new, &base, &commit_of, n_commits, args.boot, &lf)` (`paired(a, b, ..)` is the mean of a - b, as r3_compare_main's `paired(&xb, &xa, ..)` gives b - a; so diff = new - base, and lo / hi are its 2.5 / 97.5 bootstrap percentiles) and verdict `drop` if p.hi < 0.0, `gain` if p.lo > 0.0, else `same`; one line per row: `[rank-gate] label=<l> shape=<s> ranker=<r> metric=<m> base=<mean> new=<mean> diff=<+.4> ci=[<lo>, <hi>] verdict=<v>`. A gated ranker present in the run but absent from the baseline (a ranker a porting packet added to gate.json after the baseline was taken) is not judged: print `[rank-gate] new label=<l> shape=<s> ranker=<r> new_r10=<mean> new_mrr=<mean>` and count it; it enters the baselines through EG.3's declared `baseline-add`. Exit 1 if any drop (and no drift), 2 on drift or a ranker missing from the run, else 0; the last line is `[rank-gate] verdict label=<l> rows=<n> drops=<d> gains=<g> new=<w> drift=<k>`. The verdict JSON holds the rows (BTreeMap order: shape, ranker, metric); the md one table per shape (`| ranker | metric | base | new | diff [CI] | verdict |`), for the release notes.
3. Reuse `paired`, `ln_fact_table` and the JSON column reader of r3_compare_main (factor its `col` closure into `fn json_col(v: &serde_json::Value) -> Vec<f64>` and call it from both; r3_compare_main's output is unchanged). Means are plain means over queries, as `paired`'s mean. No HashMap reaches any output.

packets.risks: Same file as EG.1 (serial by the dependency). The fail rule is one-sided at the 95% level per row: with ~4 repos x 5 shapes x ~4 gated rankers x 2 metrics, a no-change run can never trip it (the diffs are exactly 0, so the CI is [0, 0]), but a real change that moves many rows raises the chance one row's CI just clears 0 by noise; the rule is the one James set ('lowers recall@10 or MRR beyond its CI'), so no multiple-comparison correction is added: open question to James. Size of the risk: only rows whose ranker actually changed can trip (unchanged rows diff exactly 0); with about 40 changed ANS rows (3-5 ANS rankers x 4 shapes x 4 repos x 2 metrics, correlated), a truly neutral reordering trips at least one row at 2.5% one-sided each with probability up to 1 - 0.975^40 = 64% if the rows were independent; correlation lowers it, and a rerun cannot clear it (the harness is deterministic). The alternative James can pick: Holm over the changed rows of one check. A drift (query set changed) cannot be judged and needs a re-baseline: EG.3's `baseline` subcommand, a declared step.

packets.title: The rank gate as a release check: bench/rank-gate/ (pinned public snapshots: glia at v0.5.2, pop-os/shell, gorilla/websocket, flutter/samples; the gated rankers; the 0.5.2 and ratcheted baselines) and scripts/rank-gate.sh fetch | run | check | baseline | baseline-add | ratchet | coverage, wired into the wave close-out
packets.area: EG rank_eval release gate: snapshots, baseline, close-out
packets.rationale: next-leap-0.5.3.md Gate: '`rank_eval` runs as a release check on fixed repo snapshots (glia plus the open-source shell / websocket / samples). A ranking change that lowers recall@10 or MRR beyond its CI fails the close-out.' Nothing at HEAD pins those snapshots: the reports name revisions only for the commons repos (round 3: commons-lang `cee7cc6b`, commons-io `11f0abe7`), and the OSS copies live in ad-hoc checkouts (/home/ivy/Code/{shell,websocket,samples}; at spec time their HEADs are shell 9616931a2f8d with 759 non-merge commits, websocket dcea2f088ce1 with 285, samples 291ba126bfc1 with 1626: exactly round 1's Repos table, so these are the revisions the reports measured). The gate must be reproducible by anyone from public sources (the repo is public; private repos never enter it), runnable by the close-out (dev-notes/wave-runner/closeout.py gates on last-line prefixes, as for scripts/check-engram-export.sh), and must compare against both the release's starting point (0.5.2: no 0.5.3 change may end below it) and the last green wave (a ratchet: a later packet may not undo an earlier gain beyond its CI).

packets.implementation:
All new files are (new) except closeout.py.
1. snapshots.json: glia {url https://github.com/James-Chahwan/glia.git, rev = 9837b1ff20bd17268db50190c91befa31227963e (`git rev-parse v0.5.2^{commit}`), flags ["--pre","glia"]}, shell {https://github.com/pop-os/shell.git, 9616931a2f8d...}, websocket {https://github.com/gorilla/websocket.git, dcea2f088ce1...}, samples {https://github.com/flutter/samples.git, 291ba126bfc1...}; expand each to 40 hex with `git -C /home/ivy/Code/<name> rev-parse HEAD` and confirm `git rev-list --no-merges --count <rev>` gives 759 / 285 / 1626 (round 1's table). Common flags for every row (in the script): `--round1 on --tune on --pick base,d85 --round2 on --round3 on --r3-perq on --ans on --max-commits 300 --max-seeds 5 --boot 1000` plus `--r1md $DIR/run/<label>.r1.md --r3md $DIR/run/<label>.r3.md`. `--pick base,d85` is round 1's harness line (dev-notes/ranking-eval-round1-2026-10-18.md: `--tune on --pick base,d85`): without it `ctx.pick` is None and PT* is P1 with sum pooling at damping 0.5, not the tuned PPR the reports measured. The md paths matter: rank_eval's defaults write rank_eval_round1.md / rank_eval_round3.md into the cwd, the repo root, which would dirty the tree and trip closeout's `uncommitted paths` gate on the next wave. The script starts with `unset GLIA_RANK_PRIVATE` and never passes `--private` (the Kina-scrub's private-config switch): the gate runs only public, Kina-free modes. Every row has `public: true`; the script refuses a row without it or with a non-https url (no private repo, no local path, ever).
2. gate.json: single [ANS:impact, ANS:pack, P1, PT*, B0, H10[PT*], H9s50, SELt2, SELs0]; k2 / k3 / half [ANS:impact, ANS:pack, P1, SELt2, SELs0] (SELs0 is item 10's structure-only selection, measured in the review shape too); find [ANS:find, T1s, SELf2t]. Before committing, check every name exists in each repo's run (EG.2's trim fails on a missing one); a name absent in one shape's bank is replaced by the nearest present reference and noted in the README. No Leiden-pooled ranker (they move with the checkout path, round 2's note). The copy's directory name `<name>@<rev12>` is part of the build identity (a copy with no .git gets RepoId `dir:<basename>`, engine/src/cache.rs ParseCache docs), so the script never renames it. gate.json also holds the coverage map `items`: one key per scope item of dev-notes/next-leap-0.5.3.md, `{"1": [], "2": [], "3": [], "4": [], "6": [], "7": [], "8": [], "10": [], "11": [], "5": {"exempt": "bit-identical scores: every existing ANS row diffing exactly 0 is its gate"}, "9": {"exempt": "link precision only, no ranking effect (round 2)"}}`; the packet that ports an item into an answer lists the gated ANS ranker(s) that measure it there (with the leak-free history its answer reads, EG.1's risks).
3. scripts/rank-gate.sh (bash, `set -uo pipefail`, the check-engram-export.sh style, every line it reports prefixed `[rank-gate]`): DIR=${GLIA_RANK_GATE_DIR:-$HOME/.cache/glia-rank-gate}. `fetch`: per row, `git clone --bare --quiet <url> $DIR/<name>.git` if absent, else `git -C .. fetch --quiet origin` only when `git cat-file -e <rev>^{commit}` fails; then the copy `$DIR/<name>@<rev12>/` by `git archive <rev> | tar -x` into a temp dir renamed into place (a `.complete` marker; an existing complete copy is reused). A fetch failure is `[rank-gate] check: FAILED (fetch <name>)`. `run`: `cargo build --release -p glia-engine --example rank_eval`, then per row `GLIA_NO_PERSIST=1 target/release/examples/rank_eval --repo <copy> --git <bare> --rev <rev> --label <label> <flags> --out $DIR/run/<label>.json --md $DIR/run/<label>.md 2> $DIR/run/<label>.log`, then `--gate-trim bench/rank-gate/gate.json --gate-new <run json> --out $DIR/run/<label>.trim.json` with GLIA_RANK_GATE_HEAD=$(git rev-parse HEAD); prints `[rank-gate] run label=<l> queries=<n> s=<wall>`. `check` (fetch + run + compare): `--gate-check` against baseline/0.5.2/<label>.json and baseline/current/<label>.json, verdicts to $DIR/run/; the last line is exactly one of `[rank-gate] check: ok - <rows> rows, <gains> gains, 0 drops on <n> snapshots`, `[rank-gate] check: FAILED (<k> drops: <label>/<shape>/<ranker>/<metric>, ..)` (exit 1) or `[rank-gate] check: FAILED (drift <label>/<shape>)` (exit 2). `baseline <release>`: run, then copy the trims to bench/rank-gate/baseline/<release>/ (a declared re-baseline; the README says only the integrator or a packet that declares it may). `ratchet`: copy the last green check's trims over baseline/current/, only those whose bytes differ (refuses unless the last check, recorded in $DIR/run/last-check.json, was ok and its GLIA_RANK_GATE_HEAD equals HEAD). `baseline-add`: for every gated ranker the last check reported `new`, merge its columns from that run's trims into both baseline/0.5.2/ and baseline/current/ (adds columns only, never rewrites an existing one; refuses when the ids differ); a declared step of the packet that adds the ranker. `coverage`: reads gate.json `items`; last line `[rank-gate] coverage: ok - <m> items measured, <e> exempt` or `[rank-gate] coverage: FAILED (unmeasured items: <list>)` (exit 1).
4. Baselines: in this packet's commit, `bash scripts/rank-gate.sh baseline 0.5.2` (the engine is still 0.5.2's ranking: no ranking packet has landed) and copy them to baseline/current/.
5. closeout.py: after the engram-export step, `out, rc = sh("bash scripts/rank-gate.sh check 2>&1", timeout=<measured glia+samples wall x 2, at least 7200>)` inside `try: .. except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:` (closeout's `sh` lets the exception escape, which would crash the close-out instead of gating) that appends `rank gate (timeout)` to gates; `say(last line)`; any last line not starting `[rank-gate] check: ok` appends `rank gate` to gates. When every gate is clean, before the commit step, `sh("bash scripts/rank-gate.sh ratchet")`, and the commit step's `git add` list gains `bench/rank-gate/baseline/current`. The step runs every wave of a release that has bench/rank-gate/gate.json (a wave whose packet commits, `git show --name-only --format= <commit>` over the journal's per-packet `commit`, touch nothing under core/, code-domain/, graph/, parsers/, engine/, activation/, bench/rank-gate/ or scripts/rank-gate.sh prints `[rank-gate] check: skipped - wave touched no ranked path` from closeout itself and is not a gate failure). The release's last close-out (closeout's `remaining` is empty) always runs `check` and then `coverage`, and a coverage line not starting `[rank-gate] coverage: ok` appends `rank gate coverage` to gates: the release cannot close with a scope item no gated answer ranker measures.

The coverage map's items are filled by the porting packets' gate packets: items 1, 2, 10 by EG.6 (with EA.9's co-change wiring), items 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 11 by EG.7.

packets.risks: Cost: four rank_eval runs with all three rounds and the ANS rankers per close-out; glia (2549 candidate files, 1253 queries) and samples (1314 files) dominate; if a check exceeds the timeout the closeout step must not be silently skipped: the timeout is a FAILED line. Network: the first fetch downloads full histories (samples is the largest); the cache is reused afterwards, and a moved or force-pushed upstream cannot change a pinned sha already fetched. Baseline size: the trims hold only the gated rankers' per-query values (estimate under 2 MB for all four); the ratchet rewrites baseline/current each green wave that changed a ranking. glia's snapshot is v0.5.2's commit, so glia's IDR (the packet JSON at each parent revision) reads only public dev-notes. Leiden-pooled rankers are excluded because they depend on the checkout path. Ordering: the 0.5.2 baseline must be captured before any ranking packet lands; the integrator schedules EG.1-EG.3 in the first waves and every ranking packet depends on EG.3. Whether the gate also fails on a drop against baseline/current (the ratchet) or only against 0.5.2 is a policy choice: this packet does both, and the 0.5.2 numbers argue for it: ANS:find is near 0 at 0.5.2, so only the ratchet can catch a later packet undoing items 3 / 6 / 11's find gain; open question to James. Who adds `053` to closeout.py's RELEASES / RELEASE_PREFIX (`"E"`) and writes schedule_053.py is the integrator's wave-runner setup, not this packet; this packet's closeout edit must merge with it. The coverage contract binds the other groups: every packet porting items 1-4, 6-8, 10 or 11 into an answer adds its ANS ranker to gate.json `items` and runs `baseline-add`; without it the release's last close-out fails by design.

packets.rationale: COMPLETENESS (integrator). EG.3's coverage contract makes the release's last close-out fail until every ranking item names a gated answer ranker with leak-free history, and no group packet filled gate.json `items`: EA.9 wires the prefix co-change into ANS:impact / ANS:pack (item 2) but names no item; items 1 (PT* / sum pooling, which reaches the answers only through selection: round 3's scope note) and 10 (structure-only selection) reach blast radius / diff-impact / review / pack only through a calibration record (EC.8, EC.9), and EG.1's ANS rankers run on copies with no record, so they always see the fallback H10. Two more facts force a new ranker rather than a record on disk: a record built from the whole history and scored on its own test commits leaks (EC verify defect 3), and EC.3's online rule already makes, at every test commit, a pick from strictly earlier test commits only. So: one in-memory calibration per snapshot run (EC.5's calibrate_snapshot over a HistorySnapshot built from rank_eval's own commit list), then every gate query of shape s at test commit c is answered by the shipped answer with its Ranking forced to the pick the record's CommitScore for (SELh0, s, c) holds (EC.1 / EC.3 integrator notes add CommitScore.sha / .pick). EA.5 adds a file-level roll-up (`files`) to blast radius, so EG.1's contract (`a packet that adds a file-level roll-up switches that answer's ANS ranker to read the roll-up`) needs a ranker reading it: ANS:impact.files; ANS:impact keeps reading rows so its 0.5.2 baseline column stays comparable.

Per seed-shape query (single = k1; k2 / k3 / half) at test commit c: pick = the SELh0 row's CommitScore for (shape, c).pick (a commit with no CommitScore: the fallback H10); `opts.ranking = Ranking::from_harness_name(pick)`, `opts.select = false` (EC.8), `opts.rank_cache = Some(cache_with_prefix)` (EA.9's per-test-commit prefix co-change, so the C0 an H10* pick reads is leak-free too); keys from `diff_impact_from_diff(..).impact.results` -> ANS:impact@sel; PackArgs the same (EC.9's `select = false`, ranking the pick) -> ANS:pack@sel. packets.rationale: COMPLETENESS (integrator). After EG.6, items 3 (intent text), 4 (calibrated selection in the text answers), 6 (IDR), 7 (LX), 8 (SELt2) and 11 (find's selection) are still unmeasured by any gated answer ranker: EG.1's ANS:find calls find_nodes (name matching, about 0 on a commit subject at 0.5.2), not EB.8's find --files that items 3 / 6 / 7 / 11 change (EC verify open question 8), and review is never called (EG.1 risk: 'a packet that changes review's ordering beyond diff impact adds an ANS:review ranker'; EB.7 / EC.11 / EC.12 do exactly that). EB.9's ENG-* rows prove the arithmetic but are parity rows, not the shipped answers. Both answers read history from the repo root (EB.3 TextIndex::load, EB.6 at the base / parent revision), and the gate copies hold no `.glia/`, so the answers need a seam that takes in-memory history, the same move EA.3's `RankCache::with_cochange` makes for co-change. Review is driven by a RevDelta the harness does not build; its intent ranking (EB.7's review_intent, EC.11's pick) is a function of (title, changed files, base revision, history), which is exactly the harness's review shape (seeds = changed files, title = the test commit's subject, base = its parent).
